questions.s: What is the smallest number by which 288 must be divided to make the quotient a perfect square?
questions.e: 288 = 12² × 2. The factor 2 has no pair, so it must be divided out to leave only complete pairs of factors. 12 is the root of the square part, not the leftover factor.

questions.s: Find the highest common factor of 48 and 36.
questions.e: Write 48 = 12 × 4 and 36 = 12 × 3. The cofactors 4 and 3 share no common factor, so the HCF is 12. 144 is the LCM of the two numbers, not their HCF.

questions.s: Which of the following decimals is the greatest?
questions.e: Compare place by place starting from tenths. In order, the numbers are 0.03, 0.033, 0.3, 0.303. 0.3 is smaller than 0.303: compare digit by digit from the first decimal place, not by the number of digits.

questions.s: What is the remainder when 3⁵⁴ is divided by 5?
questions.e: The remainders of 3, 3², 3³, … on division by 5 are 3, 4, 2, 1 and then repeat, with a cycle of 4. Since 54 = 4 × 13 + 2, the remainder is the one at position 2 in the cycle, 4.

questions.s: The five-digit number 187x9, where x is a single digit, is divisible by 9. What is the value of x?
questions.e: A number is divisible by 9 when its digit sum is a multiple of 9. Putting x = 2 gives 18,729 = 9 × 2,081; no other digit works.

questions.s: A rectangular floor measures 175 cm by 200 cm. What is the side of the largest square tile that fits exactly, without cutting, along both sides?
questions.e: The tile side must divide both 175 and 200, and be as large as possible, so it is their HCF = 25 cm. 1,400 cm is the LCM; the tile must divide both lengths, so the HCF is needed.

questions.s: How many numbers from 96 to 306, both included, are exactly divisible by 8?
questions.e: Multiples of 8 up to 306: 38. Multiples below 96: 11. So 38 − 11 = 27. 26 can miss a multiple at the start; count multiples up to 306 minus multiples below 96.

questions.s: What is the unit digit of 7²⁹?
questions.e: The unit digits of powers of 7 repeat in a cycle of length 4: 7, 9, 3, 1. Since 29 = 4 × 7 + 1, the unit digit is number 1 in the cycle: 7.

questions.s: A rectangular floor measures 540 cm by 420 cm. What is the side of the largest square tile that fits exactly, without cutting, along both sides?
questions.e: The tile side must divide both 540 and 420, and be as large as possible, so it is their HCF = 60 cm. 3,780 cm is the LCM; the tile must divide both lengths, so the HCF is needed.

questions.s: The HCF of two numbers is 5 and their product is 1,050. What is their LCM?
questions.e: For two numbers, HCF × LCM = product. So LCM = 1,050 ÷ 5 = 210. 5,250 multiplies by the HCF instead of dividing.

questions.s: Which of the following fractions is the greatest?
questions.e: Over the common denominator 72, the fractions are 32/72, 54/72, 9/72, 27/72. The largest numerator belongs to 3/4. 4/9 is smaller than 3/4, as the common denominator shows.

questions.s: Three alarm clocks go off at intervals of 12, 15 and 20 minutes and have just sounded together. After how many minutes will they next sound together?
questions.e: They coincide at common multiples of the intervals, and the first is the LCM of 12, 15 and 20, which is 60. 3,600 minutes is a common multiple but not the least one.

questions.s: Evaluate: √11.56
questions.e: 11.56 = 1156 ÷ 100, and √1156 = 34, √100 = 10. The root is 34 ÷ 10 = 3.4. 34 has the decimal point one place too far right: the root has half as many decimal places as the number.

questions.s: A number leaves remainder 9 when divided by 11, and another number leaves remainder 2. What is the remainder when their sum is divided by 11?
questions.e: Add the remainders: 9 + 2 = 11. This is equal to 11, so subtract 11 to get 0. 11 is not smaller than the divisor, so it has not yet been reduced.

questions.s: Which of the following numbers is exactly divisible by 3?
questions.e: A number is divisible by 3 when its digit sum is a multiple of 3. Only 111 passes (111 = 3 × 37); each of the others leaves a remainder.

questions.s: Three alarm clocks go off at intervals of 20, 25 and 30 minutes and have just sounded together. After how many minutes will they next sound together?
questions.e: They coincide at common multiples of the intervals, and the first is the LCM of 20, 25 and 30, which is 300. 3,000 minutes is a common multiple but not the least one.

questions.s: The decimal 0.3111… (the digit 1 repeating after the first decimal place) is equal to the fraction
questions.e: Let x = 0.311…. Then 10x = 3.11… and 100x = 31.11…. Subtracting, 90x = 28, so x = 14/45. 31/99 treats both digits as repeating.

questions.s: The five-digit number 15x71, where x is a single digit, is divisible by 9. What is the value of x?
questions.e: A number is divisible by 9 when its digit sum is a multiple of 9. Putting x = 4 gives 15,471 = 9 × 1,719; no other digit works.

questions.s: How many prime numbers lie between 75 and 96?
questions.e: Test each number from 76 to 95 for divisors up to its square root. The primes in this range are 79, 83, 89, which makes 3.

questions.s: How many prime numbers lie between 32 and 56?
questions.e: Test each number from 33 to 55 for divisors up to its square root. The primes in this range are 37, 41, 43, 47, 53, which makes 5.

questions.s: What is the least number that must be subtracted from 3,763 so that the result is exactly divisible by 15?
questions.e: 3,763 ÷ 15 leaves remainder 13, so subtracting 13 gives the multiple of 15 just below it. 2 is the number to add, not to subtract.

questions.s: What is the sum of all the positive factors of 60?
questions.e: List the factors in pairs: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 60. Their sum is 168. 12 is the number of factors, not their sum.

questions.s: Evaluate: √9.61
questions.e: 9.61 = 961 ÷ 100, and √961 = 31, √100 = 10. The root is 31 ÷ 10 = 3.1. 31 has the decimal point one place too far right: the root has half as many decimal places as the number.

questions.s: What is the sum of all multiples of 3 from 3 to 75?
questions.e: The multiples are 3 × (1 + 2 + … + 25) = 3 × 325 = 975. 325 is the sum of 1 to 25; each term must be multiplied by 3.

questions.s: Which of the following numbers is exactly divisible by 8?
questions.e: A number is divisible by 8 when its last three digits form a number divisible by 8. Only 928 passes (928 = 8 × 116); each of the others leaves a remainder.

questions.s: What is the greatest four-digit number exactly divisible by 10, 15 and 25?
questions.e: The LCM of 10, 15 and 25 is 150. Dividing 9,999 by 150 leaves remainder 99, so subtract it: 9,999 − 99 = 9,900. 9,999 is the greatest four-digit number but it leaves a remainder.

questions.s: Hira has Rs 100. She spends 2/5 of it on books and 1/2 of the remainder on food. How much money is left with her?
questions.e: After books she has Rs 60. Food takes 1/2 of this, leaving 1/2 of Rs 60, which is Rs 30. Rs 10 subtracts both fractions from the whole amount, but the second fraction is of the remainder only.

questions.s: What is the least number that must be added to 2,221 so that the sum is exactly divisible by 13?
questions.e: 2,221 ÷ 13 leaves remainder 11. To reach the next multiple of 13, add 13 − 11 = 2. 11 is the remainder; adding it moves away from the next multiple.

questions.s: What is 5/6 of 1/2 of 60?
questions.e: 'Of' means multiply: 5/6 × 1/2 × 60 = 25. 50 takes only the first fraction.

questions.s: Which fraction is equal to the decimal 0.185?
questions.e: 0.185 = 185/1,000, which reduces to 37/200 after dividing top and bottom by 5. 37/2000 has one decimal place too many in the denominator; the denominator must be 1 followed by as many zeros as there are decimal places.

questions.s: Evaluate: 0.7 × 0.9
questions.e: Multiply as whole numbers (7 × 9) and then restore the decimal places: the factors have 2 in total, giving 0.63. 6.3 has one decimal place too few: the number of decimal places in the product equals the total in the factors.

questions.s: What is the sum of the first 29 odd natural numbers?
questions.e: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n². Here n = 29, so the sum is 841. 870 is the sum of the first 29 even numbers.

questions.s: Which of the following numbers is exactly divisible by 4?
questions.e: A number is divisible by 4 when its last two digits form a number divisible by 4. Only 232 passes (232 = 4 × 58); each of the others leaves a remainder.

questions.s: What is the HCF of the fractions 2/5, 2/9, 8/27?
questions.e: HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators ÷ LCM of denominators (fractions in lowest terms). Here HCF(2, 2, 8) = 2 and LCM(5, 9, 27) = 135, giving 2/135. 8 swaps the rules: the HCF of fractions is HCF of numerators over LCM of denominators.

questions.s: What is the sum of all the positive factors of 72?
questions.e: List the factors in pairs: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 72. Their sum is 195. 12 is the number of factors, not their sum.

questions.s: What is the LCM of 12 and 18?
questions.e: 12 = 6 × 2 and 18 = 6 × 3, so LCM = 6 × 2 × 3 = 36. 216 is just the product 12 × 18; the numbers share the factor 6, so the product is not the least common multiple.

questions.s: What is the smallest four-digit number exactly divisible by 14, 21 and 6?
questions.e: The LCM of 14, 21 and 6 is 42. The first multiple of 42 that reaches 1,000 is 1,008. 966 is a multiple of 42 but has only three digits.

questions.s: Evaluate: (−3)⁴ + (−2)² + (−4)³
questions.e: A negative number to an even power is positive and to an odd power is negative. Evaluating each term separately gives 81 + 4 + (−64) = 21. −149 treats (−x)ⁿ as −xⁿ; with an even power the bracket makes the result positive.

questions.s: Evaluate: 4½ − 3⅖
questions.e: Change to improper fractions: 9/2 − 17/5 = 11/10, which is 1 1/10 as a mixed number.

questions.s: The sum of three consecutive even numbers is 72. What is the smallest of them?
questions.e: The middle number is the average: 72 ÷ 3 = 24. The numbers are 22, 24, 26, so the smallest is 22. 24 is the middle number; the middle term equals the average, not the smallest one.

questions.s: How many positive factors does 108 have?
questions.e: Prime factorisation: 108 = 2² × 3³. The number of factors is (2+1) × (3+1) = 12. 5 only adds the exponents; each exponent must first be increased by 1 and the results multiplied.

questions.s: The sum of five consecutive integers is 85. What is the largest of them?
questions.e: The middle number is the average: 85 ÷ 5 = 17. The numbers are 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, so the largest is 19. 17 is the middle number; the middle term equals the average, not the largest one.

questions.s: The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their product is 3,024. What is their LCM?
questions.e: For two numbers, HCF × LCM = product. So LCM = 3,024 ÷ 12 = 252. 36,288 multiplies by the HCF instead of dividing.

questions.s: What is the greatest number that divides 91, 151 and 199 leaving the same remainder in each case?
questions.e: If two numbers leave the same remainder on division by m, m divides their difference. The differences are 60 and 48, whose HCF is 12. 1 is the HCF of the numbers themselves and would leave remainder 0; it is not the HCF of their differences.

questions.s: Which fraction is equal to the decimal 0.82?
questions.e: 0.82 = 82/100, which reduces to 41/50 after dividing top and bottom by 2. 41/500 has one decimal place too many in the denominator; the denominator must be 1 followed by as many zeros as there are decimal places.

questions.s: Which of the following fractions is the smallest?
questions.e: Over the common denominator 330, the fractions are 231/330, 220/330, 30/330, 264/330. The smallest numerator belongs to 1/11. 7/10 is larger than 1/11, as the common denominator shows.

questions.s: What is the sum of the natural numbers from 1 to 67?
questions.e: Use n(n+1)/2 = 67 × 68 ÷ 2 = 2278. 4,556 is double the sum; divide by 2.

questions.s: Evaluate: 17 + 8 × 6 − 49 ÷ 7
How many positive factors does 360 have?
questions.e: Prime factorisation: 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5. The number of factors is (3+1) × (2+1) × (1+1) = 24. 6 only adds the exponents; each exponent must first be increased by 1 and the results multiplied.

questions.s: What is the smallest number greater than 1 which leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 12, 15 or 20?
questions.e: The number must be 1 more than a common multiple of 12, 15 and 20. Their LCM is 60, so the smallest such number is 60 + 1 = 61. 60 is the LCM itself and leaves remainder 0, not 1.

questions.s: What is the sum of all the positive factors of 30?
questions.e: List the factors in pairs: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. Their sum is 72. 8 is the number of factors, not their sum.

questions.s: What is the greatest number that divides 157, 165 and 205 leaving the same remainder in each case?
questions.e: If two numbers leave the same remainder on division by m, m divides their difference. The differences are 8 and 40, whose HCF is 8. 1 is the HCF of the numbers themselves and would leave remainder 0; it is not the HCF of their differences.

questions.s: Which of the following decimals is the smallest?
questions.e: Compare place by place starting from tenths. In order, the numbers are 0.02, 0.2, 0.202, 0.27. 0.2 is larger than 0.02: compare digit by digit from the first decimal place, not by the number of digits.

questions.s: What is the HCF of the fractions 2/3, 2/9, 20/27?
questions.e: HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators ÷ LCM of denominators (fractions in lowest terms). Here HCF(2, 2, 20) = 2 and LCM(3, 9, 27) = 27, giving 2/27. 20/3 swaps the rules: the HCF of fractions is HCF of numerators over LCM of denominators.

questions.s: A number leaves remainder 6 when divided by 8, and another number leaves remainder 4. What is the remainder when their sum is divided by 8?
questions.e: Add the remainders: 6 + 4 = 10. This is more than 8, so subtract 8 to get 2. 10 is not smaller than the divisor, so it has not yet been reduced.

questions.s: Simplify: 1/3 + 1/6
questions.e: Use the common denominator 6: 2/6 + 1/6 = 1/2. 2/9 comes from combining numerators and denominators separately, which is not how fractions are combined.

questions.s: When 198 and 192 are each divided by 13, the remainders are 3 and 10. What is the remainder when their product is divided by 13?
questions.e: The remainder of a product depends only on the remainders: 3 × 10 = 30, and 30 leaves remainder 4 on division by 13. 30 is larger than the divisor; it must itself be reduced by 13.

questions.s: How many positive factors does 144 have?
questions.e: Prime factorisation: 144 = 2⁴ × 3². The number of factors is (4+1) × (2+1) = 15. 6 only adds the exponents; each exponent must first be increased by 1 and the results multiplied.

questions.s: Fatima has Rs 960. She spends 3/8 of it on books and 1/3 of the remainder on food. How much money is left with her?
questions.e: After books she has Rs 600. Food takes 1/3 of this, leaving 2/3 of Rs 600, which is Rs 400. Rs 280 subtracts both fractions from the whole amount, but the second fraction is of the remainder only.

questions.s: The recurring decimal 0.878787… (with the digits 87 repeating) is equal to the fraction
questions.e: Let x = 0.8787…. Then 100x − x = 87, so x = 87/99 = 29/33. 87/100 is the terminating decimal 0.87; a two-digit repeating block needs denominator 99.

questions.s: Evaluate: 5⅖ + 3⅔
questions.e: Change to improper fractions: 27/5 + 11/3 = 136/15, which is 9 1/15 as a mixed number. 8½ adds numerators and denominators separately.

questions.s: What is the smallest number greater than 2 which leaves a remainder of 2 when divided by 8, 12 or 18?
questions.e: The number must be 2 more than a common multiple of 8, 12 and 18. Their LCM is 72, so the smallest such number is 72 + 2 = 74. 72 is the LCM itself and leaves remainder 0, not 2.

questions.s: What is the smallest number by which 2,016 must be divided to make the quotient a perfect square?
questions.e: 2,016 = 12² × 14. The factor 14 has no pair, so it must be divided out to leave only complete pairs of factors. 12 is the root of the square part, not the leftover factor.

questions.s: Find the least common multiple of 18 and 10.
questions.e: 18 = 2 × 9 and 10 = 2 × 5, so LCM = 2 × 9 × 5 = 90. 180 is just the product 18 × 10; the numbers share the factor 2, so the product is not the least common multiple.

questions.s: Evaluate: 3.1 ÷ 0.01
questions.e: Multiply both numbers by 100 to make the divisor whole: this leaves the quotient unchanged and gives 310. 31 has the decimal point in the wrong place; dividing by a number less than 1 makes the result larger than the dividend.

questions.s: The decimal 0.2333… (the digit 3 repeating after the first decimal place) is equal to the fraction
questions.e: Let x = 0.233…. Then 10x = 2.33… and 100x = 23.33…. Subtracting, 90x = 21, so x = 7/30. 23/99 treats both digits as repeating.

questions.s: What is the greatest number that divides 119, 128 and 173 leaving the same remainder in each case?
questions.e: If two numbers leave the same remainder on division by m, m divides their difference. The differences are 9 and 45, whose HCF is 9. 1 is the HCF of the numbers themselves and would leave remainder 0; it is not the HCF of their differences.

questions.s: Evaluate: (8 + 11) × 7 − 4²
questions.e: Brackets first: 8 + 11 = 19. Then 19 × 7 = 133 and 4² = 16, giving 117. 69 ignores the brackets, which must be worked out first.

questions.s: Evaluate: 0.5 × 0.05
questions.e: Multiply as whole numbers (5 × 5) and then restore the decimal places: the factors have 3 in total, giving 0.025. 0.25 has one decimal place too few: the number of decimal places in the product equals the total in the factors.

questions.s: Evaluate: 9 + 3 × 8 − 45 ÷ 9
What is the LCM of 14, 15 and 4?
questions.e: Take the highest power of each prime in the factorisations of 14, 15 and 4. This gives 420, the smallest number all three divide into. 210 is divisible by only some of 14, 15 and 4, so it is not their common multiple.

questions.s: The greatest number that divides both 28 and 21 exactly is
questions.e: Write 28 = 7 × 4 and 21 = 7 × 3. The cofactors 4 and 3 share no common factor, so the HCF is 7. 84 is the LCM of the two numbers, not their HCF.

questions.s: Simplify: 4/5 − 1/2
questions.e: Use the common denominator 10: 8/10 − 5/10 = 3/10. 1 comes from combining numerators and denominators separately, which is not how fractions are combined.

questions.s: A rectangular floor measures 420 cm by 300 cm and is covered with the largest possible square tiles, none cut. How many tiles are needed?
questions.e: The largest tile has side HCF(420, 300) = 60 cm. Along the sides there are 7 and 5 tiles, so 7 × 5 = 35 tiles. 12 counts tiles along the two sides added together, not the full area covered.

questions.s: Which fraction is equal to the decimal 0.804?
questions.e: 0.804 = 804/1,000, which reduces to 201/250 after dividing top and bottom by 4. 201/2500 has one decimal place too many in the denominator; the denominator must be 1 followed by as many zeros as there are decimal places.

questions.s: Zainab's monthly income is 20% more than Rabia's. By what percentage is Rabia's income less than Zainab's?
questions.e: Let Rabia earn 100. Then Zainab earns 120. The difference of 20 is 20/120 of Zainab's income, which is 16⅔%. 20% reverses the base: the difference is now measured against the larger amount, so the percentage changes.

questions.s: The price of a packet of biscuits changes from Rs 200 to Rs 150. What is the percentage decrease in price?
questions.e: Change = 50. Percentage decrease = 50 ÷ 200 × 100 = 25%. 33⅓% divides the change by the new price; the percentage change is always taken on the original price.

questions.s: The price of an item falls by 20%. By what percentage must the quantity bought increase so that the total spending stays the same?
questions.e: New price is 80% of the old, so quantity must become 100/80 of the old, an increase of 25%. 20% ignores that the quantity is now measured against a smaller base price.

questions.s: What is 12.5% of 320?
questions.e: 12.5% of 320 = 12.5 ÷ 100 × 320 = 40. 4 has the decimal point in the wrong place: x% of y is x × y ÷ 100.

questions.s: The pass rate of a college rose from 50% to 65%. By what percentage did the pass rate itself increase?
questions.e: The rise is 65 − 50 = 15 percentage points. Compared with the original 50%, that is 15 ÷ 50 × 100 = 30%. 15% is the rise in percentage points, not the percentage increase.

questions.s: Nida's savings are 80% of Amna's savings, and Amna's savings are 50% of Sana's savings. Nida's savings are what percentage of Sana's?
questions.e: Take Sana's savings as 100. Then Amna's = 50 and Nida's = 80% of 50 = 40. So Nida's savings are 40% of Sana's. 130% adds the percentages, but they should be multiplied as fractions.

questions.s: If 25% of a number is equal to 10% of 500, what is the number?
questions.e: Let the number be n. Then 25/100 × n = 10/100 × 500, so n = 10 × 500 ÷ 25 = 200. 1,250 swaps the percentages.

questions.s: After a 10% raise, a clerk's salary is Rs 15,400 per month. What was the salary before the change?
questions.e: New value = original × 110/100. So original = 15,400 × 100 ÷ 110 = 14,000. Rs 13,860 applies the percentage to the new figure; it is 10% of the original, not of the new value.

questions.s: If 60% of a number is equal to 36% of 600, what is the number?
questions.e: Let the number be n. Then 60/100 × n = 36/100 × 600, so n = 36 × 600 ÷ 60 = 360. 1,000 swaps the percentages.

questions.s: The length of a rectangle is increased by 10% and its breadth is decreased by 20%. What is the effect on its area?
questions.e: Area is length × breadth. The scale factor is 110/100 × 80/100 = 22/25, so the area shows a 12% decrease. 10% decrease subtracts the percentages directly, missing the interaction term xy/100.

questions.s: A bicycle is bought for Rs 25,000 and its value falls by 20% every year. What is its value after 2 years?
questions.e: Multiply by 4/5 each year: 25,000 × (4/5)² = 16,000. Rs 15,000 uses the same amount each year; each year's change applies to the value at the start of that year.

questions.s: What is 50% of 60% of 2,000?
questions.e: 60% of 2,000 = 1,200; then 50% of that = 600. 2,200 adds the two percentages instead of applying them one after the other.

questions.s: A number exceeds its 20% by 224. What is the number?
questions.e: The number minus 20% of it is 80% of it, so 80% of the number = 224. Number = 224 × 100 ÷ 80 = 280. 1,120 treats 224 as 20% of the number; it is the difference between the number and its 20%.

questions.s: In an examination, 75% of the candidates passed Chemistry, 55% passed Computer Science and 50% passed both subjects. What percentage of the candidates failed in both subjects?
questions.e: Passed at least one subject = 75 + 55 − 50 = 80% (the overlap is counted once). Failed both = 100 − 80 = 20%. 50% is the percentage who did not pass both, which includes those who passed one subject.

questions.s: A school has 500 students. Of these, 60% are girls, and 20% of the girls study science. How many girls study science?
questions.e: Girls = 60% of 500 = 300. Science girls = 20% of 300 = 60. 300 is the number of girls, not those studying science.

questions.s: A restaurant bill including 20% tax comes to Rs 1,920. What was the bill before tax?
questions.e: Total = 120% of the pre-tax bill, so pre-tax bill = 1,920 × 100 ÷ 120 = 1,600. Rs 1,536 takes 20% off the total, but the tax was added to the pre-tax amount, so the total is 120% of it.

questions.s: A family's monthly income is Rs 50,000 and its expenditure is Rs 40,000. If income rises by 10% and expenditure rises by 5%, by what percentage do the monthly savings increase?
questions.e: Original savings = 50,000 − 40,000 = 10,000. New income = 55,000, new expenditure = 42,000, so new savings = 13,000. Increase = 3,000 ÷ 10,000 × 100 = 30%. 5% subtracts the two rates, but the savings are the difference of two different amounts, so the rates cannot be subtracted directly.

questions.s: In an entrance test, 24 of 50 candidates from Lahore passed, and 75 of 100 candidates from Multan passed. Which city had the higher pass percentage, and by how much?
questions.e: Lahore: 24/50 = 48%. Multan: 75/100 = 75%. Multan is higher by 27 percentage points. Lahore, by 27 percentage points names the wrong city: compare the percentages, not the raw numbers who passed.

questions.s: The radius of a circular pizza is increased by 50%. By what percentage does its area increase?
questions.e: Area is proportional to r². With r from 100 to 150, r² goes from 10,000 to 22,500, an increase of 125%. 50% is the increase in the radius; area depends on the square of the radius.

questions.s: The population of a village is 10,000 and it grows by 10% every year. What will the population be after 2 years?
questions.e: Multiply by 11/10 each year: 10,000 × (11/10)² = 12,100. 12,000 uses the same amount each year; each year's change applies to the value at the start of that year.

questions.s: Sana attended 84 of the first 120 classes of a course. There are 60 classes left. To finish with 80% attendance overall, how many of the remaining classes must she attend?
questions.e: Total classes = 120 + 60 = 180. 80% of 180 = 144. She has 84 already, so she needs 144 − 84 = 60 more. 48 takes 80% of the remaining classes only, ignoring what has already been attended.

questions.s: Saima scored 26 out of 50, 40 out of 50, 54 out of 100 in 3 papers. What is her overall percentage?
questions.e: Total obtained = 120 and total maximum = 200. Overall percentage = 120 ÷ 200 × 100 = 60%. 62% is the plain average of the separate percentages; papers with more marks must count for more.

questions.s: The price of a ticket for a bus journey changes from Rs 400 to Rs 700. What is the percentage increase in price?
questions.e: Change = 300. Percentage increase = 300 ÷ 400 × 100 = 75%. 42.86% divides the change by the new price; the percentage change is always taken on the original price.

questions.s: In a two-candidate election, the winner received 58% of the valid votes and won by 3,680 votes. How many valid votes were polled?
questions.e: The winner got 58% and the other candidate 42%, so the margin is 16% of the valid votes. Valid votes = 3,680 × 100 ÷ 16 = 23,000. 13,340 is the number of votes the winner received, not the total.

questions.s: A shopkeeper gives successive discounts of 25% and 50% on an article. What single discount is equal to these two discounts?
questions.e: A price of 100 becomes 100 × 75/100 × 50/100 = 37.5, so the single discount is 100 − 37.5 = 62.5%. 75% just adds the discounts; the second discount is on the reduced price, so the total is smaller.

questions.s: Maryam scored 44 out of 50, 30 out of 50, 85 out of 100 in 3 papers. What is her overall percentage?
questions.e: Total obtained = 159 and total maximum = 200. Overall percentage = 159 ÷ 200 × 100 = 79.5%. 77⅔% is the plain average of the separate percentages; papers with more marks must count for more.

questions.s: Imran's monthly pocket money is Rs 560. He saves 75% of it. How much does he save each month?
questions.e: 75% of 560 = 75 ÷ 100 × 560 = 420. Rs 42 has the decimal point in the wrong place: x% of y is x × y ÷ 100.

questions.s: Express 28% as a fraction in its lowest terms.
questions.e: 28% = 28/100 = 7/25 after reducing to lowest terms. 14/5 puts the percentage over 10 instead of 100: x% means x/100.

questions.s: Express 62.5% as a fraction in its lowest terms.
questions.e: 62.5% = 62.5/100 = 5/8 after reducing to lowest terms. 1/16 puts the percentage over 1,000 instead of 100: x% means x/100.

questions.s: In a class of 40 students, 55% are girls. How many boys are there in the class?
questions.e: Girls = 55% of 40 = 22. The remaining students are boys: 40 − 22 = 18. 22 is the number of girls, not the number of boys.

questions.s: What is 40% of 680?
questions.e: 40% of 680 = 40 ÷ 100 × 680 = 272. 2,720 has the decimal point in the wrong place: x% of y is x × y ÷ 100.

questions.s: What percentage of 20 is 18?
questions.e: Percentage = part ÷ whole × 100 = 18 ÷ 20 × 100 = 90%. 111.11% divides the other way round; the part goes on top: part ÷ whole × 100.

questions.s: The number of customers in a bakery is increased by 20% and the new value is then decreased by 20%. What is the net effect?
questions.e: Take 100 as the original value: after +20% it is 120; after −20% it is 96. The net change is 4% decrease. No change just subtracts the percentages; the decrease is applied to the increased value, not to the original.

questions.s: A shirt marked at Rs 1,000 is sold at a 12% discount. What is the price payable?
questions.e: Price = 1,000 × 88/100 = 880. Rs 1,120 takes the discount the wrong way round: it should be taken off.

questions.s: The radius of a circular pizza is increased by 10%. By what percentage does its area increase?
questions.e: Area is proportional to r². With r from 100 to 110, r² goes from 10,000 to 12,100, an increase of 21%. 10% is the increase in the radius; area depends on the square of the radius.

questions.s: Maryam attended 42 of the first 60 classes of a course. There are 50 classes left. To finish with 80% attendance overall, how many of the remaining classes must she attend?
questions.e: Total classes = 60 + 50 = 110. 80% of 110 = 88. She has 42 already, so she needs 88 − 42 = 46 more. 40 takes 80% of the remaining classes only, ignoring what has already been attended.

questions.s: To pass an examination, a candidate needs 35% of the maximum marks. Sana scored 325 marks and failed by 25 marks. What are the maximum marks?
questions.e: Pass mark = 325 + 25 = 350, which is 35% of the maximum. So maximum = 350 × 100 ÷ 35 = 1,000. 350 is the pass mark, not the maximum marks.

questions.s: An 80 kg salt solution contains 10% salt. How many kilograms of water must be evaporated so that the solution becomes 20% salt?
questions.e: Salt = 10% of 80 = 8 kg, which does not change. In the final solution this is 20%, so the mass is 8 × 100 ÷ 20 = 40 kg. Water evaporated = 80 − 40 = 40 kg. 8 kg subtracts the percentages and applies the difference to the original mass, but the salt must stay fixed.

questions.s: Which of the following is the greatest?
questions.e: Work out each value: 30% of 580 = 174, 25% of 140 = 35, 75% of 620 = 465, 45% of 260 = 117. The largest is 75% of 620. 30% of 580 is smaller than 75% of 620; the biggest percentage or the biggest number alone does not decide it.

questions.s: The price of a packet of biscuits changes from Rs 360 to Rs 378. What is the percentage increase in price?
questions.e: Change = 18. Percentage increase = 18 ÷ 360 × 100 = 5%. 4.76% divides the change by the new price; the percentage change is always taken on the original price.

questions.s: After a discount of 15%, a pair of shoes is sold for Rs 850. What is the marked price?
questions.e: The sale price is 85% of the marked price, so marked price = 850 × 100 ÷ 85 = 1,000.

questions.s: Express 17/200 as a percentage.
questions.e: 17/200 × 100 = 8.5%. 0.85% has the decimal point one place too far left: multiply the fraction by 100.

questions.s: To pass an examination, a candidate needs 50% of the maximum marks. Nida scored 230 marks and failed by 20 marks. What are the maximum marks?
questions.e: Pass mark = 230 + 20 = 250, which is 50% of the maximum. So maximum = 250 × 100 ÷ 50 = 500. 250 is the pass mark, not the maximum marks.

questions.s: What is 60% of 25% of 1,200?
questions.e: 25% of 1,200 = 300; then 60% of that = 180. 1,020 adds the two percentages instead of applying them one after the other.

questions.s: Danish's salary is 20% more than Hamza's, and Hamza's salary is 20% less than Usman's. Danish's salary is what percentage less than Usman's?
questions.e: Take Usman's salary as 100. Then Hamza's is 80 and Danish's is 120% of 80 = 96. So Danish's is 4% less than Usman's.

questions.s: In a class of 400 students, 70% are girls. How many boys are there in the class?
questions.e: Girls = 70% of 400 = 280. The remaining students are boys: 400 − 280 = 120. 280 is the number of girls, not the number of boys.

questions.s: The value of a share changes in three successive months by −10%, −25%, +50%. What is the net change over the three months?
questions.e: Multiply the factors: 90/100 × 75/100 × 150/100 = 1.0125. So the net change is 1.25% increase. 15% increase adds the percentages, but each change applies to the value left by the previous one.

questions.s: A school has 200 students. Of these, 45% are girls, and 20% of the girls study science. How many girls study science?
questions.e: Girls = 45% of 200 = 90. Science girls = 20% of 90 = 18. 90 is the number of girls, not those studying science.

questions.s: Evaluate: 25% of 280 + 40% of 660
questions.e: 25% of 280 = 70 and 40% of 660 = 264. So the value is 70 + 264 = 334. 611 combines the percentages and the numbers before multiplying, which is not valid.

questions.s: Evaluate: 30% of 320 + 25% of 180
questions.e: 30% of 320 = 96 and 25% of 180 = 45. So the value is 96 + 45 = 141. 275 combines the percentages and the numbers before multiplying, which is not valid.

questions.s: A 150 kg salt solution contains 8% salt. How many kilograms of water must be evaporated so that the solution becomes 10% salt?
questions.e: Salt = 8% of 150 = 12 kg, which does not change. In the final solution this is 10%, so the mass is 12 × 100 ÷ 10 = 120 kg. Water evaporated = 150 − 120 = 30 kg. 3 kg subtracts the percentages and applies the difference to the original mass, but the salt must stay fixed.

questions.s: Which of the following is the smallest?
questions.e: Work out each value: 75% of 600 = 450, 10% of 520 = 52, 45% of 140 = 63, 60% of 660 = 396. The smallest is 10% of 520. 75% of 600 is larger than 10% of 520; the biggest percentage or the biggest number alone does not decide it.

questions.s: The price of a electric iron, after a 40% reduction, is Rs 600. What was the original price?
questions.e: New value = original × 60/100. So original = 600 × 100 ÷ 60 = 1,000. Rs 840 applies the percentage to the new figure; it is 40% of the original, not of the new value.

questions.s: Express 51/80 as a percentage.
questions.e: 51/80 × 100 = 63.75%. 6.38% has the decimal point one place too far left: multiply the fraction by 100.

questions.s: The price of a mobile phone is increased by 25% and the new value is then decreased by 30%. What is the net effect?
questions.e: Take 100 as the original value: after +25% it is 125; after −30% it is 87.5. The net change is 12.5% decrease. 5% decrease just subtracts the percentages; the decrease is applied to the increased value, not to the original.

questions.s: The price of flour rises by 150%. By what percentage must a family cut its consumption so that its monthly spending on flour stays the same?
questions.e: Spending = price × quantity. New price is 250% of the old, so the quantity must fall to 100/250 of the old, a cut of 60%. 150% would be right only if the price had fallen; the cut is measured against the larger amount used before.

questions.s: Ahmed's salary is 40% more than Faisal's, and Faisal's salary is 25% less than Zubair's. Ahmed's salary is what percentage more than Zubair's?
questions.e: Take Zubair's salary as 100. Then Faisal's is 75 and Ahmed's is 140% of 75 = 105. So Ahmed's is 5% more than Zubair's. 15% just subtracts the percentages, but each percentage is taken on a different base.

questions.s: Iqra's monthly salary is Rs 60,000. She spends 20% on rent and 50% of the remainder on food, and saves the rest. How much does she save?
questions.e: After rent, Rs 60,000 × 80% = Rs 48,000. Food takes 50% of this, leaving 50% = Rs 24,000. Rs 18,000 subtracts both percentages from the salary, but the food share is 50% of what is left after rent only.

questions.s: A family's monthly income is Rs 60,000 and its expenditure is Rs 45,000. If income rises by 20% and expenditure rises by 10%, by what percentage do the monthly savings increase?
questions.e: Original savings = 60,000 − 45,000 = 15,000. New income = 72,000, new expenditure = 49,500, so new savings = 22,500. Increase = 7,500 ÷ 15,000 × 100 = 50%. 10% subtracts the two rates, but the savings are the difference of two different amounts, so the rates cannot be subtracted directly.

questions.s: The pass rate of a college rose from 40% to 60%. By what percentage did the pass rate itself increase?
questions.e: The rise is 60 − 40 = 20 percentage points. Compared with the original 40%, that is 20 ÷ 40 × 100 = 50%. 20% is the rise in percentage points, not the percentage increase.

questions.s: A number exceeds its 30% by 210. What is the number?
questions.e: The number minus 30% of it is 70% of it, so 70% of the number = 210. Number = 210 × 100 ÷ 70 = 300. 700 treats 210 as 30% of the number; it is the difference between the number and its 30%.

questions.s: In an examination, 80% of the candidates passed Chemistry, 55% passed Computer Science and 45% passed both subjects. What percentage of the candidates failed in both subjects?
questions.e: Passed at least one subject = 80 + 55 − 45 = 90% (the overlap is counted once). Failed both = 100 − 90 = 10%. 55% is the percentage who did not pass both, which includes those who passed one subject.

questions.s: In a two-candidate election, 5% of the votes polled were invalid. The winner got 55% of the valid votes and won by 950 votes. How many votes were polled in all?
questions.e: Margin = (55 − 45)% = 10% of valid votes, so valid votes = 950 × 100 ÷ 10 = 9,500. These are 95% of the votes polled, so total = 9,500 × 100 ÷ 95 = 10,000. 9,500 is the number of valid votes; the total polled includes the invalid ones.

questions.s: Express 37.5% as a fraction in its lowest terms.
questions.e: 37.5% = 37.5/100 = 3/8 after reducing to lowest terms. 3/80 puts the percentage over 1,000 instead of 100: x% means x/100.

questions.s: In a two-candidate election, the winner received 65% of the valid votes and won by 600 votes. How many valid votes were polled?
questions.e: The winner got 65% and the other candidate 35%, so the margin is 30% of the valid votes. Valid votes = 600 × 100 ÷ 30 = 2,000. 1,300 is the number of votes the winner received, not the total.

questions.s: The value of a share changes in three successive months by −10%, +50%, +10%. What is the net change over the three months?
questions.e: Multiply the factors: 90/100 × 150/100 × 110/100 = 1.485. So the net change is 48.5% increase. 50% increase adds the percentages, but each change applies to the value left by the previous one.

questions.s: A bill of Rs 3,800 has 10% sales tax added. What is the total payable?
questions.e: Total = 3,800 × 110/100 = 4,180. Rs 3,420 takes the tax the wrong way round: it should be added.

questions.s: What percentage of 200 is 129?
questions.e: Percentage = part ÷ whole × 100 = 129 ÷ 200 × 100 = 64.5%. 155.04% divides the other way round; the part goes on top: part ÷ whole × 100.

questions.s: Hamza's marks are 75% less than Imran's. By what percentage are Imran's marks more than Hamza's?
questions.e: Let Imran score 100. Then Hamza scores 25. The difference 75 compared with 25 is 300%. 75% repeats the same percentage, but the difference must now be measured against the smaller amount.

questions.s: What is 40% of 20% of 1,000?
questions.e: 20% of 1,000 = 200; then 40% of that = 80. 600 adds the two percentages instead of applying them one after the other.

questions.s: In an entrance test, 100 of 125 candidates from Lahore passed, and 40 of 100 candidates from Multan passed. Which city had the higher pass percentage, and by how much?
questions.e: Lahore: 100/125 = 80%. Multan: 40/100 = 40%. Lahore is higher by 40 percentage points. Multan, by 40 percentage points names the wrong city: compare the percentages, not the raw numbers who passed.

questions.s: Mehwish's savings are 60% of Saima's savings, and Saima's savings are 80% of Hira's savings. Mehwish's savings are what percentage of Hira's?
questions.e: Take Hira's savings as 100. Then Saima's = 80 and Mehwish's = 60% of 80 = 48. So Mehwish's savings are 48% of Hira's. 140% adds the percentages, but they should be multiplied as fractions.

questions.s: A shopkeeper gives successive discounts of 15% and 25% on an article. What single discount is equal to these two discounts?
questions.e: A price of 100 becomes 100 × 85/100 × 75/100 = 63.75, so the single discount is 100 − 63.75 = 36.25%. 40% just adds the discounts; the second discount is on the reduced price, so the total is smaller.

questions.s: Hira's monthly salary is Rs 40,000. She spends 40% on rent and 25% of the remainder on food, and saves the rest. How much does she save?
questions.e: After rent, Rs 40,000 × 60% = Rs 24,000. Food takes 25% of this, leaving 75% = Rs 18,000. Rs 14,000 subtracts both percentages from the salary, but the food share is 25% of what is left after rent only.

questions.s: The price of a refrigerator, after a 20% increase, is Rs 16,800. What was the original price?
questions.e: New value = original × 120/100. So original = 16,800 × 100 ÷ 120 = 14,000. Rs 13,440 applies the percentage to the new figure; it is 20% of the original, not of the new value.

questions.s: Which of the following ratios is the greatest?
questions.e: Write each ratio as a fraction over a common denominator: 180/495, 396/495, 275/495, 90/495. The largest is 4 : 5. 4 : 11 is smaller than 4 : 5.

questions.s: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 7. When 12 is added to each, the ratio becomes 45 : 89. What is the larger number?
questions.e: Let the numbers be 3x and 7x. Then (3x + 12) : (7x + 12) = 45 : 89, so 89(3x + 12) = 45(7x + 12), which gives x = 11. The larger number is 7 × 11 = 77. 33 is the smaller number.

questions.s: Rs 900 is divided into three parts so that the first : second = 2 : 1 and the second : third = 4 : 3. What is the second part?
questions.e: Make the second part common: first : second : third = 8 : 4 : 3. One part = 900 ÷ 15 = 60, so the second part is 4 × 60 = 240. 300 is one-third of the total, but the parts are not equal.

questions.s: Find x if 4 : 9 = 20 : x.
questions.e: From 4 : 9 = 20 : x we get 4x = 9 × 20, so x = 180 ÷ 4 = 45. 25 uses addition; a ratio statement needs multiplication.
Cross-multiply: 4(x + 2) = 3(x + 8), so 4x + 8 = 3x + 24, giving 1x = 16 and x = 16. 6 cross-multiplies only the x-terms and drops the constants.

questions.s: A printer prints 48 pages in 8 minutes. How many pages will it print in 26 minutes at the same rate?
questions.e: Rate = 48 ÷ 8 = 6 per unit of time. For 26: 6 × 26 = 156. 66 adds the extra time as if each unit gave one more item.

questions.s: The speeds of Kamran and Danish are in the ratio 4 : 5. If Kamran takes 60 minutes to cover a certain distance, how long does Danish take to cover the same distance?
questions.e: For the same distance, time is inversely proportional to speed, so the times are in the ratio 5 : 4. Danish's time = 60 × 4 ÷ 5 = 48 minutes. 75 minutes treats time as directly proportional to speed; the faster person takes less time.

questions.s: A container holds 75 litres of pure milk. 15 litres are removed and replaced with water, and the same operation is then repeated once more. How many litres of milk are left in the container?
questions.e: After the first step milk = 75 − 15 = 60 litres, which is 4/5 of the container. After the second step milk = 75 × (4/5)² = 48 litres. 45 litres subtracts 15 litres twice, but the second removal takes out a mixture that is partly water.

questions.s: The fourth proportional to 6, 10 and 30 is
questions.e: From 6 : 10 = 30 : x we get 6x = 10 × 30, so x = 300 ÷ 6 = 50. 18 multiplies the wrong pair: x = (second × third) ÷ first.

questions.s: Rs 1,200 is divided among Maryam, Sana and Ayesha. Maryam gets 1/2 of what Sana gets, and Sana gets 2/3 of what Ayesha gets. How much does Ayesha get?
questions.e: Take Ayesha = 1. Then Sana = 2/3 and Maryam = 1/2 × 2/3 = 1/3. In whole numbers Maryam : Sana : Ayesha = 1 : 2 : 3. One part = 1,200 ÷ 6 = Rs 200, so Ayesha gets 3 × 200 = Rs 600. Rs 400 is Sana's share.

questions.s: Which of the following ratios is equal to 20 : 24?
questions.e: Divide both terms by 4: 20 : 24 = 5 : 6. 6 : 7 adds to both terms; equal ratios come from dividing or multiplying both terms by the same number.

questions.s: Tea costing Rs 50 per kg is mixed with tea costing Rs 80 per kg to make a mixture worth Rs 70 per kg. In what ratio (cheaper : dearer) must they be mixed?
questions.e: By alligation, cheaper : dearer = (dearer price − mean) : (mean − cheaper price) = (80 − 70) : (70 − 50) = 10 : 20, i.e. 1 : 2. 2 : 1 is reversed: the cheaper kind is taken in proportion to (dearer price − mean), not (mean − cheaper price).

questions.s: The monthly incomes of Ahmed and Bilal are in the ratio 7 : 5, and their monthly expenditures are in the ratio 5 : 3. Each saves Rs 4,000 a month. What is Ahmed's income?
questions.e: Let incomes be 7x and 5x and expenditures 5y and 3y. Then 7x − 5y = 4,000 and 5x − 3y = 4,000. Solving gives x = 2,000 and y = 2,000, so Ahmed's income is 7 × 2,000 = Rs 14,000. Rs 10,000 is Bilal's income.

questions.s: Rs 740 is divided into three parts so that the first : second = 1 : 3 and the second : third = 4 : 7. What is the first part?
questions.e: Make the second part common: first : second : third = 4 : 12 : 21. One part = 740 ÷ 37 = 20, so the first part is 4 × 20 = 80. 100 is one-third of the total, but the parts are not equal.

questions.s: A 64-litre mixture of milk and water has milk and water in the ratio 5 : 3. How many litres of water must be added to make the ratio 5 : 4?
questions.e: Milk = 40 litres, water = 24 litres. Milk stays the same, so for 5 : 4 the water must be 32 litres. Water to add = 32 − 24 = 8 litres. 32 litres is the total water needed, not the extra water to add.

questions.s: The sum of the present ages of Amna and Iqra is 28 years, and their ages are in the ratio 3 : 4. What was Iqra's age 4 years ago?
questions.e: One part = 28 ÷ 7 = 4. Iqra's present age = 4 × 4 = 16, so 4 years ago she was 16 − 4 = 12. 16 years is Iqra's present age, not her age 4 years ago.

questions.s: Mixture A of milk and water has the ratio 1 : 4 and Mixture B has the ratio 1 : 2. If 10 litres of A and 30 litres of B are mixed, what is the ratio of milk to water in the new mixture?
questions.e: Milk in A = 2 L and water = 8 L. Milk in B = 10 L and water = 20 L. Total milk = 12 L and total water = 28 L, so the ratio is 12 : 28, i.e. 3 : 7. 1 : 3 adds the ratio terms directly; the quantities of A and B must be taken into account.
Cross-multiply: 5(x + 5) = 4(x + 12), so 5x + 25 = 4x + 48, giving 1x = 23 and x = 23.

questions.s: The ages of Asad and Rabia are in the ratio 4 : 5. If Rabia is 45 years old, how old is Asad?
questions.e: One part = 45 ÷ 5 = 9. The other number = 4 × 9 = 36.

questions.s: Rs 5,000 is divided among Nida, Mehwish and Zubair in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. How much does Mehwish get?
questions.e: Total parts = 10, so one part = 5,000 ÷ 10 = Rs 500. Mehwish gets 3 parts = Rs 1,500. Rs 500 is the value of one part, not of Mehwish's share.

questions.s: 8 workers can dig a water channel in 20 days. How many days would 40 workers take to do the same work at the same rate?
questions.e: Total work = 8 × 20 = 160 worker-days. With 40 workers: 160 ÷ 40 = 4 days. 100 days treats workers and days as directly proportional; more workers should need fewer days.

questions.s: What is the compound ratio of 7 : 1 and 7 : 1?
questions.e: The compound ratio multiplies antecedents and consequents: (7 × 7) : (1 × 1) = 49 : 1. 7 : 1 adds the terms; a compound ratio multiplies them.

questions.s: What is the mean proportional between 1 and 16?
questions.e: If x is the mean proportional, x² = 1 × 16 = 16, so x = √16 = 4.

questions.s: Express the ratio 4 hours to 250 minutes in its simplest form.
questions.e: Convert to the same unit: 4 hours = 240 minutes. The ratio is 240 : 250, which simplifies to 24 : 25. 2 : 125 compares the numbers without converting to the same unit.

questions.s: The sum of the present ages of Zainab and Hira is 77 years, and their ages are in the ratio 4 : 7. What was Hira's age 3 years ago?
questions.e: One part = 77 ÷ 11 = 7. Hira's present age = 7 × 7 = 49, so 3 years ago she was 49 − 3 = 46. 49 years is Hira's present age, not her age 3 years ago.

questions.s: The money with Rabia and Fatima is in the ratio 7 : 5. When Rabia gives Rs 250 to Fatima, the ratio becomes 17 : 15. How much money did Rabia have originally?
questions.e: Let the amounts be 7x and 5x. Then (7x − 250) : (5x + 250) = 17 : 15, so 15(7x − 250) = 17(5x + 250). Solving gives x = 400, so Rabia had 7 × 400 = Rs 2,800. Rs 2,000 is the amount Fatima had originally.

questions.s: The monthly incomes of Ahmed and Bilal are in the ratio 5 : 4, and their monthly expenditures are in the ratio 3 : 2. Each saves Rs 1,500 a month. What is Ahmed's income?
questions.e: Let incomes be 5x and 4x and expenditures 3y and 2y. Then 5x − 3y = 1,500 and 4x − 2y = 1,500. Solving gives x = 750 and y = 750, so Ahmed's income is 5 × 750 = Rs 3,750. Rs 3,000 is Bilal's income.

questions.s: A map has a scale of 1 : 100,000. Two villages are 15 cm apart on the map. What is the actual distance between them in kilometres?
questions.e: Actual distance = 15 × 100,000 = 1,500,000 cm. Since 1 km = 100,000 cm, this is 15 km. 150 km is out by a factor of 10: 1 km = 100,000 cm.

questions.s: Rs 5,950 is divided among Rabia and Mehwish in the ratio 3 : 4. How much does Rabia get?
questions.e: Total parts = 7, so one part = 5,950 ÷ 7 = Rs 850. Rabia gets 3 parts = Rs 2,550. Rs 850 is the value of one part, not of Rabia's share.

questions.s: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 3 : 2, and there are 36 boys. How many students are there in the class?
questions.e: 3 parts = 36, so one part = 12. Total parts = 5, so the class has 5 × 12 = 60 students. 24 is the number of girls.

questions.s: The ages of Amna and Rabia are in the ratio 3 : 8. After 10 years the ratio of their ages will be 8 : 13. What is Rabia's present age?
questions.e: Let the present ages be 3x and 8x. Then (3x + 10) : (8x + 10) = 8 : 13, so 13(3x + 10) = 8(8x + 10), which gives x = 2. Rabia's age is 8 × 2 = 16. 26 is Rabia's age after 10 years, not now.

questions.s: A recipe needs rice and lentils in the ratio 5 : 3. If 55 kg of rice is used, how many kg of lentils are needed?
questions.e: One part = 55 ÷ 5 = 11 kg. Lentils needed = 3 × 11 = 33 kg.

questions.s: Kamran invests Rs 30,000 and Bilal invests Rs 50,000 in a business for the same period. The profit is Rs 40,000. What is Bilal's share of the profit?
questions.e: Profit is shared in the ratio of investments 3 : 5. Bilal gets 5 of 8 parts: Rs 40,000 × 5 ÷ 8 = Rs 25,000. Rs 20,000 splits the profit equally, ignoring the amounts invested.

questions.s: Which of the following ratios is equal to 24 : 54?
questions.e: Divide both terms by 6: 24 : 54 = 4 : 9. 5 : 10 adds to both terms; equal ratios come from dividing or multiplying both terms by the same number.

questions.s: 12 workers can dig a water channel in 10 days. How many days would 20 workers take to do the same work at the same rate?
questions.e: Total work = 12 × 10 = 120 worker-days. With 20 workers: 120 ÷ 20 = 6 days.

questions.s: A 36-litre mixture of milk and water has milk and water in the ratio 7 : 2. How many litres of water must be added to make the ratio 7 : 4?
questions.e: Milk = 28 litres, water = 8 litres. Milk stays the same, so for 7 : 4 the water must be 16 litres. Water to add = 16 − 8 = 8 litres. 16 litres is the total water needed, not the extra water to add.
Cross-multiply: 4(x + 3) = 3(x + 6), so 4x + 12 = 3x + 18, giving 1x = 6 and x = 6.

questions.s: If x : y = 7 : 4, what is (x + y) : (x − y)?
questions.e: Put x = 7k and y = 4k. Then x + y = 11k and x − y = 3k, so the ratio is 11 : 3. 3 : 11 is the ratio the wrong way round.

questions.s: A bus covers 150 km in 5 hours at a steady speed. How far will it travel in 15 hours at the same speed?
questions.e: Speed = 150 ÷ 5 = 30 km/h. Distance in 15 hours = 30 × 15 = 450 km. 50 km treats distance and time as inversely related; at a fixed speed they increase together.

questions.s: A 20-litre mixture of milk and water has milk and water in the ratio 4 : 1. How many litres of water must be added to make the ratio 4 : 3?
questions.e: Milk = 16 litres, water = 4 litres. Milk stays the same, so for 4 : 3 the water must be 12 litres. Water to add = 12 − 4 = 8 litres. 12 litres is the total water needed, not the extra water to add.

questions.s: Food for 80 residents of a hostel lasts 24 days. After 15 days, 20 of them leave. For how many more days will the remaining food last the others?
questions.e: Total food = 80 × 24 = 1,920 person-days. After 15 days 1,200 person-days are used, leaving 720. Now 60 remain, so the food lasts 720 ÷ 60 = 12 more days. 9 days forgets that fewer people eat the remaining food, so it lasts longer.

questions.s: The radii of two circles are in the ratio 4 : 5. What is the ratio of their areas?
questions.e: Area is proportional to r², so the ratio is 4² : 5² = 16 : 25. 4 : 5 is just the ratio of the lengths; areas and volumes scale with powers.

questions.s: If 15 bottles of juice cost Rs 375, what is the cost of 21 bottles of juice at the same rate?
questions.e: Cost of one = 375 ÷ 15 = Rs 25. For 21: 25 × 21 = Rs 525. Rs 381 adds the extra items as if each cost Rs 1.

questions.s: The speeds of Bilal and Ahmed are in the ratio 4 : 3. If Bilal takes 36 minutes to cover a certain distance, how long does Ahmed take to cover the same distance?
questions.e: For the same distance, time is inversely proportional to speed, so the times are in the ratio 3 : 4. Ahmed's time = 36 × 4 ÷ 3 = 48 minutes. 27 minutes treats time as directly proportional to speed; the faster person takes less time.

questions.s: What is the compound ratio of 1 : 9 and 5 : 6?
questions.e: The compound ratio multiplies antecedents and consequents: (1 × 5) : (9 × 6) = 5 : 54. 2 : 5 adds the terms; a compound ratio multiplies them.

questions.s: The ages of Nida and Fatima are in the ratio 5 : 7. After 8 years the ratio of their ages will be 7 : 9. What is Fatima's present age?
questions.e: Let the present ages be 5x and 7x. Then (5x + 8) : (7x + 8) = 7 : 9, so 9(5x + 8) = 7(7x + 8), which gives x = 4. Fatima's age is 7 × 4 = 28. 36 is Fatima's age after 8 years, not now.

questions.s: What is the mean proportional between 27 and 75?
questions.e: If x is the mean proportional, x² = 27 × 75 = 2,025, so x = √2,025 = 45. 51 is the arithmetic mean; the mean proportional is the geometric mean √(ab).

questions.s: Ayesha invests Rs 25,000 and Danish invests Rs 35,000 in a business for the same period. The profit is Rs 30,000. What is Danish's share of the profit?
questions.e: Profit is shared in the ratio of investments 5 : 7. Danish gets 7 of 12 parts: Rs 30,000 × 7 ÷ 12 = Rs 17,500. Rs 15,000 splits the profit equally, ignoring the amounts invested.

questions.s: Zainab invests Rs 12,000 for 6 months and Naveed invests Rs 18,000 for 12 months in a business. The profit is Rs 24,000. What is Zainab's share?
questions.e: Profit is shared in the ratio of investment × time: 12,000 × 6 : 18,000 × 12 = 1 : 3. Zainab's share = Rs 24,000 × 1 ÷ 4 = Rs 6,000. Rs 9,600 ignores the time for which the money was invested.

questions.s: If A : B = 1 : 7 and B : C = 7 : 3, what is A : C?
questions.e: Make B equal in both: A : B = 7 : 49 and B : C = 49 : 21. Then A : C = 7 : 21, i.e. 1 : 3. 3 : 49 multiplies the wrong terms.

questions.s: Iqra and Ayesha share some money in the ratio 5 : 8. Ayesha's share is Rs 1,800 more than Iqra's. How much money did they share?
questions.e: The difference of 3 parts is Rs 1,800, so one part = Rs 600. Total = 13 parts = Rs 7,800. Rs 23,400 multiplies the difference by the total parts instead of dividing by the difference in parts.

questions.s: Sana and Nida share some money in the ratio 3 : 7. Nida's share is Rs 1,200 more than Sana's. How much money did they share?
questions.e: The difference of 4 parts is Rs 1,200, so one part = Rs 300. Total = 10 parts = Rs 3,000. Rs 12,000 multiplies the difference by the total parts instead of dividing by the difference in parts.

questions.s: A container holds 36 litres of pure milk. 6 litres are removed and replaced with water, and the same operation is then repeated once more. How many litres of milk are left in the container?
questions.e: After the first step milk = 36 − 6 = 30 litres, which is 5/6 of the container. After the second step milk = 36 × (5/6)² = 25 litres. 24 litres subtracts 6 litres twice, but the second removal takes out a mixture that is partly water.

questions.s: What is the third proportional to 5 and 15?
questions.e: The third proportional x satisfies 5 : 15 = 15 : x, so x = 15² ÷ 5 = 45. 75 is the product of the two numbers; the third proportional x satisfies a : b = b : x.

questions.s: 4 workers earn Rs 4,800 in 3 days. At the same rate, how much will 10 workers earn in 4 days?
questions.e: Earnings depend on workers × days. Each worker-day earns Rs 4,800 ÷ (4 × 3) = Rs 400. For 10 × 4 = 40 worker-days: 40 × 400 = Rs 16,000. Rs 12,000 accounts for the number of workers only, not the number of days.

questions.s: The edges of two cubes are in the ratio 3 : 4. What is the ratio of their volumes?
questions.e: Volume is proportional to the cube of the edge, so the ratio is 3³ : 4³ = 27 : 64. 3 : 4 is just the ratio of the lengths; areas and volumes scale with powers.

questions.s: Which of the following ratios is the smallest?
questions.e: Write each ratio as a fraction over a common denominator: 90/165, 110/165, 66/165, 99/165. The smallest is 2 : 5. 6 : 11 is larger than 2 : 5.

questions.s: A recipe needs flour and sugar in the ratio 5 : 2. If 45 kg of flour is used, how many kg of sugar are needed?
questions.e: One part = 45 ÷ 5 = 9 kg. Sugar needed = 2 × 9 = 18 kg.

questions.s: Two numbers are in the ratio 4 : 9. If the first number is 24, what is the second number?
questions.e: One part = 24 ÷ 4 = 6. The other number = 9 × 6 = 54.

questions.s: Express the ratio 2.25 kilometres to 25 metres in its simplest form.
questions.e: Convert to the same unit: 2.25 kilometres = 2,250 metres. The ratio is 2,250 : 25, which simplifies to 90 : 1. 9 : 100 compares the numbers without converting to the same unit.

questions.s: A bag contains coins of Rs 1, Rs 2 and Rs 5 in the ratio 3 : 2 : 1. The total value of the coins is Rs 24. How many Rs 5 coins are there?
questions.e: One ratio unit has 3 Rs 1, 2 Rs 2 and 1 Rs 5 coins, worth 3 + 4 + 5 = Rs 12. Units = 24 ÷ 12 = 2, so Rs 5 coins = 1 × 2 = 2. 10 is the value of the Rs 5 coins in rupees, not their number.

questions.s: Tea costing Rs 200 per kg is mixed with tea costing Rs 230 per kg to make a mixture worth Rs 210 per kg. In what ratio (cheaper : dearer) must they be mixed?
questions.e: By alligation, cheaper : dearer = (dearer price − mean) : (mean − cheaper price) = (230 − 210) : (210 − 200) = 20 : 10, i.e. 2 : 1. 1 : 2 is reversed: the cheaper kind is taken in proportion to (dearer price − mean), not (mean − cheaper price).

questions.s: Mixture A of milk and water has the ratio 3 : 1 and Mixture B has the ratio 4 : 1. If 20 litres of A and 10 litres of B are mixed, what is the ratio of milk to water in the new mixture?
questions.e: Milk in A = 15 L and water = 5 L. Milk in B = 8 L and water = 2 L. Total milk = 23 L and total water = 7 L, so the ratio is 23 : 7. 7 : 2 adds the ratio terms directly; the quantities of A and B must be taken into account.

questions.s: Rs 4,200 is divided among Hamza and Zubair in the ratio 2 : 5. How much does Zubair get?
questions.e: Total parts = 7, so one part = 4,200 ÷ 7 = Rs 600. Zubair gets 5 parts = Rs 3,000. Rs 600 is the value of one part, not of Zubair's share.

questions.s: What is the third proportional to 3 and 9?
questions.e: The third proportional x satisfies 3 : 9 = 9 : x, so x = 9² ÷ 3 = 27. 15 continues the numbers as an arithmetic pattern, not a proportion.

questions.s: The sum of the present ages of Hira and Zainab is 64 years, and their ages are in the ratio 3 : 5. What was Zainab's age 3 years ago?
questions.e: One part = 64 ÷ 8 = 8. Zainab's present age = 5 × 8 = 40, so 3 years ago she was 40 − 3 = 37. 40 years is Zainab's present age, not her age 3 years ago.

questions.s: A tailor stitches 30 shirts in 6 days. How many shirts will he stitch in 12 days at the same rate?
questions.e: Rate = 30 ÷ 6 = 5 per unit of time. For 12: 5 × 12 = 60. 15 treats the amount and the time as inversely related; at a steady rate they increase together.

questions.s: On a map, 1 cm represents 2 km. Two towns are 6.4 cm apart on the map. What is the actual distance between them?
questions.e: Actual distance = 6.4 × 2 = 12.8 km. 3.2 km divides instead of multiplying.

questions.s: Food for 200 soldiers lasts 24 days. After 12 days, 50 of them leave. For how many more days will the remaining food last the others?
questions.e: Total food = 200 × 24 = 4,800 person-days. After 12 days 2,400 person-days are used, leaving 2,400. Now 150 remain, so the food lasts 2,400 ÷ 150 = 16 more days. 12 days forgets that fewer people eat the remaining food, so it lasts longer.

questions.s: A bag contains coins of Rs 1, Rs 2 and Rs 5 in the ratio 10 : 5 : 2. The total value of the coins is Rs 240. How many Rs 5 coins are there?
questions.e: One ratio unit has 10 Rs 1, 5 Rs 2 and 2 Rs 5 coins, worth 10 + 10 + 10 = Rs 30. Units = 240 ÷ 30 = 8, so Rs 5 coins = 2 × 8 = 16. 80 is the value of the Rs 5 coins in rupees, not their number.

questions.s: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 3 : 1, and there are 30 boys. How many students are there in the class?
questions.e: 3 parts = 30, so one part = 10. Total parts = 4, so the class has 4 × 10 = 40 students. 10 is the number of girls.

questions.s: The money with Mehwish and Saima is in the ratio 5 : 3. When Mehwish gives Rs 400 to Saima, the ratio becomes 3 : 5. How much money did Mehwish have originally?
questions.e: Let the amounts be 5x and 3x. Then (5x − 400) : (3x + 400) = 3 : 5, so 5(5x − 400) = 3(3x + 400). Solving gives x = 200, so Mehwish had 5 × 200 = Rs 1,000. Rs 600 is the amount Saima had originally.

questions.s: On a map, 1 cm represents 20 km. Two towns are 12 cm apart on the map. What is the actual distance between them?
questions.e: Actual distance = 12 × 20 = 240 km. 0.6 km divides instead of multiplying.

questions.s: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 4. When 8 is added to each, the ratio becomes 19 : 24. What is the larger number?
questions.e: Let the numbers be 3x and 4x. Then (3x + 8) : (4x + 8) = 19 : 24, so 24(3x + 8) = 19(4x + 8), which gives x = 10. The larger number is 4 × 10 = 40. 30 is the smaller number.

questions.s: If A : B = 4 : 1 and B : C = 6 : 7, what is A : B : C?
questions.e: Make B equal: A : B = 24 : 6 and B : C = 6 : 7. So A : B : C = 24 : 6 : 7. 4 : 6 : 7 puts the original numbers side by side without making B equal in both ratios.

questions.s: What is the mean of 12, 15, 18, 21 and 24?
questions.e: Sum = 12 + 15 + 18 + 21 + 24 = 90 and 90 ÷ 5 = 18. The sum (90) forgets to divide by the number of values; 15 is just the second value, not the mean.

questions.s: Bilal scored 40, 55, 35, 60, 45 and 50 marks in six class tests. What is his average mark?
questions.e: Total = 285 over 6 tests, so the average is 285 ÷ 6 = 47.5. Dividing by 5 ignores one of the six tests.

questions.s: What is the average of the first 20 natural numbers?
questions.e: The sum of 1 to 20 is 20 × 21 ÷ 2 = 210, so the mean is 210 ÷ 20 = 10.5. Stopping at 10 or rounding to 11 loses the half; the mean of 1 to n is (n + 1)/2.

questions.s: The average of five numbers is 24. What is their sum?
questions.e: Sum = average × count = 24 × 5 = 120. Adding 24 and 5 or dividing 24 by 5 does not undo the averaging step; 96 is only four times the average.

questions.s: The mean of 8 numbers is 15. A ninth number, 24, is added. What is the new mean?
questions.e: Old sum = 8 × 15 = 120, so the new sum is 120 + 24 = 144 over 9 numbers: 144 ÷ 9 = 16. Averaging 15 and 24 (19.5) gives the old mean and the new number equal weight, but the old mean stands for 8 numbers.

questions.s: What is the average of 3.5, 4.5 and 7.0?
questions.e: Sum = 15 and 15 ÷ 3 = 5. The middle value 4.5 is the median, not the mean.

questions.s: The average of 6 numbers is 20. One of them, 8, is removed. What is the average of the remaining five?
questions.e: Total = 6 × 20 = 120. After removing 8 the total is 112 over 5 numbers: 112 ÷ 5 = 22.4. Because 8 is below the mean, removing it must raise the average, so 20 and 18.5 cannot be right.

questions.s: What is the mean of the even numbers 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 14?
questions.e: Sum = 56 and 56 ÷ 7 = 8. The numbers are evenly spaced, so the mean equals the middle number, 8. The value 7 is the count of numbers.

questions.s: The average age of three friends is 21 years. Two of them are 18 and 22 years old. How old is the third?
questions.e: Total age = 3 × 21 = 63 and the known ages sum to 40, so the third friend is 63 − 40 = 23 years old. Answering 21 mistakes the mean for the missing value.

questions.s: A shopkeeper in Multan sells 120, 150, 90, 140 and 100 kg of rice on five days. What is the mean daily sale?
questions.e: Total = 120 + 150 + 90 + 140 + 100 = 600 kg. Over 5 days that is 600 ÷ 5 = 120 kg per day. 600 kg is the five-day total.

questions.s: The average of 7 consecutive integers is 30. What is the largest of them?
questions.e: For consecutive integers the mean is the middle (4th) term, so the 4th is 30 and the 7th is 30 + 3 = 33. Adding 6 or 7 counts from the first term instead of the middle one.

questions.s: The sum of 15 numbers is 465. What is their average?
questions.e: Average = 465 ÷ 15 = 31. The value 46.5 comes from dividing by 10 instead of by the 15 numbers.

questions.s: The mean mark of 30 students in section A is 60 and of 20 students in section B is 70. What is the mean mark of all 50 students?
questions.e: Total = 30 × 60 + 20 × 70 = 1,800 + 1,400 = 3,200, and 3,200 ÷ 50 = 64. The simple average 65 treats the two sections as equal in size, but section A has more students, so the combined mean sits nearer 60.

questions.s: The average weight of 8 boys is 45 kg. When a new boy joins, the average becomes 46 kg. What is the weight of the new boy?
questions.e: New total = 9 × 46 = 414 kg and old total = 8 × 45 = 360 kg, so the new boy weighs 54 kg. He adds 1 kg to each of the 9 boys' average and also covers the 9 kg gap between his weight and the old mean of 45 kg.

questions.s: The average of 10 numbers is 40. One number was copied as 25 when it should have been 52. What is the correct average?
questions.e: The wrong total is 10 × 40 = 400. The correct total is 400 − 25 + 52 = 427, so the correct mean is 42.7. Keeping 40 ignores the correction; 37.3 subtracts 27 instead of adding it.

questions.s: The mean of five numbers is 18. Each number is multiplied by 3 and then 2 is added to each. What is the new mean?
questions.e: Multiplying every value by 3 multiplies the mean by 3 to give 54, and adding 2 to every value raises the mean by 2 to give 56. The value 54 skips the addition; 60 adds before multiplying, which is the wrong order.

questions.s: Ayesha's average in four tests is 72. What must she score in the fifth test to make her five-test average 75?
questions.e: Needed total = 75 × 5 = 375 and she has 72 × 4 = 288 so far, so she needs 375 − 288 = 87. A score of 75 does not make up the shortfall of 3 marks on each of the first four tests.

questions.s: The average of 11 numbers is 50. The average of the first six is 49 and of the last six is 52. What is the sixth number?
questions.e: The sixth number belongs to both groups. First six total 294 and last six total 312, so together they give 606, which is the total of all 11 (550) plus the sixth number counted a second time. Hence the sixth is 606 − 550 = 56.

questions.s: The average age of a cricket team of 11 players is 28 years. If the captain, aged 35, is excluded, what is the average age of the remaining 10?
questions.e: Total age = 11 × 28 = 308. Without the captain it is 308 − 35 = 273 over 10 players, which is 27.3 years. The mean would stay at 28 only if the captain were also 28.

questions.s: A train covers a journey in two equal-distance halves: the first half at 40 km/h and the second half at 60 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
questions.e: For equal distances, average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 2 × 40 × 60 ÷ (40 + 60) = 4,800 ÷ 100 = 48 km/h. The simple mean 50 would apply only if equal times were spent at each speed; here more time is spent at the slower speed.

questions.s: The average of four consecutive even numbers is 17. What is the smallest of them?
questions.e: Four consecutive even numbers are symmetric about their mean, so they are 14, 16, 18, 20. Check: 68 ÷ 4 = 17. Starting at 16 gives 16, 18, 20, 22, whose mean is 19.

questions.s: The average height of 20 girls in a class is 150 cm and the average height of all 50 students is 156 cm. What is the average height of the 30 boys?
questions.e: Total height = 50 × 156 = 7,800 cm and the girls account for 20 × 150 = 3,000 cm. The boys total 4,800 cm, so their mean is 4,800 ÷ 30 = 160 cm. It cannot be 156 cm, since the girls pull the class mean below the boys' mean.

questions.s: The average monthly salary of 20 employees in an office is Rs 30,000. When the manager's salary is added, the average rises by Rs 1,000. What is the manager's monthly salary?
questions.e: New total = 21 × 31,000 = 651,000 and old total = 20 × 30,000 = 600,000, so the manager earns Rs 51,000. Taking 20 × 1,000 = 20,000 above the old mean gives Rs 50,000 and forgets that the manager also needs to reach the new mean of Rs 31,000.

questions.s: The average of x, x + 2, x + 4, x + 6 and x + 8 is 20. What is x?
questions.e: The five terms are evenly spaced, so their mean is the middle term: x + 4 = 20, which gives x = 16. Setting x = 20 treats the first term as the mean.

questions.s: The mean of the first three of four numbers is 12 and the mean of the last three is 15. If the last number is 18, what is the first number?
questions.e: The first three sum to 36 and the last three sum to 45. The two sums share the middle two numbers, so they differ by (last − first): 45 − 36 = 9 = 18 − first, giving first = 9.

questions.s: A class of 40 students has a recorded average mark of 62. Three marks of 70, 65 and 55 were wrongly entered as 48, 58 and 44. What is the corrected average?
questions.e: The three marks were under-entered by 22 + 7 + 11 = 40 in total. Corrected total = 2,480 + 40 = 2,520, and 2,520 ÷ 40 = 63. Leaving the average at 62 keeps the error.

questions.s: A batsman has an average of 40 runs after 10 innings. How many runs must he score in his 11th innings to raise his average to 42?
questions.e: Needed total = 11 × 42 = 462 and he has 10 × 40 = 400, so he needs 62. Scoring 42 only matches the target; it does not make up the 2 runs per earlier innings by which he is below it.

questions.s: The average of five numbers is 27. One number is removed and the average of the other four becomes 25. What number was removed?
questions.e: Total of five = 5 × 27 = 135 and total of four = 4 × 25 = 100, so the removed number is 135 − 100 = 35. Guessing 29 from 27 + 2 ignores the change in the number of values.

questions.s: The mean of 12 numbers is 9. Three of them have a mean of 6. What is the mean of the other nine?
questions.e: Total = 12 × 9 = 108 and the three numbers total 18, so the other nine total 90 and their mean is 10. The mean cannot stay at 9, because the removed values are below it.

questions.s: Rukhsana's marks in four subjects average 68. Her marks in the first two subjects average 62. What is her average in the last two subjects?
questions.e: Total = 4 × 68 = 272 and the first two total 124, so the last two total 148 and their mean is 74. Both groups have two subjects, so the means balance around 68: 62 is 6 below, hence the other must be 6 above.

questions.s: A factory makes 600, 720 and 840 units per hour in consecutive periods lasting 2, 3 and 5 hours respectively. What is the mean output per hour over the 10 hours?
questions.e: Weighted by hours: 600 × 2 + 720 × 3 + 840 × 5 = 1,200 + 2,160 + 4,200 = 7,560 units, and 7,560 ÷ 10 = 756 per hour. The simple mean 720 ignores that the fastest period lasted longest.

questions.s: A cyclist rides for 2 hours at 12 km/h and then for 3 hours at 18 km/h. What is his average speed over the 5 hours?
questions.e: Distance = 2 × 12 + 3 × 18 = 24 + 54 = 78 km in 5 hours, so the average speed is 78 ÷ 5 = 15.6 km/h. The simple mean 15 ignores that he rode longer at the faster speed.

questions.s: Five years ago the average age of a family of 4 was 26 years. A baby has since been born, and the average age of the family of 5 today is 25 years. How old is the baby today?
questions.e: Today the four older members have total age 4 × 26 + 4 × 5 = 124, since each has aged 5 years. The family of five totals 5 × 25 = 125, so the baby is 125 − 124 = 1 year old. Using the old total of 104 instead would give 21, which ignores that the older members have aged.

questions.s: The average of nine numbers is 36. The average of the first five is 34 and of the last five is 38. What is the fifth number?
questions.e: The fifth number is in both groups, so (first five total) + (last five total) = 170 + 190 = 360 equals the total of all nine (324) plus the fifth number again. Hence the fifth is 360 − 324 = 36.

questions.s: The mean of 50 numbers is 38. Two of the numbers, 45 and 55, are removed. What is the mean of the remaining 48 numbers?
questions.e: Total = 50 × 38 = 1,900. Removing 45 + 55 = 100 leaves 1,800 over 48 numbers, and 1,800 ÷ 48 = 37.5. The removed numbers average 50, which is above 38, so the mean must fall, but only by 0.5.

questions.s: In a class of 30 students the average mark of the boys is 50 and of the girls is 65. If the class average is 56, how many boys are there?
questions.e: Let there be b boys. Then 50b + 65(30 − b) = 56 × 30, so 1,950 − 15b = 1,680, giving b = 18. Check by distances: 56 is 6 above 50 and 9 below 65, so boys : girls = 9 : 6 = 3 : 2, which is 18 : 12.

questions.s: The average of a, b and c is 16. Given that the average of a and b is 14 and the average of b and c is 17, what is the value of b?
questions.e: a + b + c = 48, a + b = 28 and b + c = 34. Adding the last two gives a + 2b + c = 62, and subtracting the total 48 gives b = 14. Check: a = 14 and c = 20, and the mean is 48 ÷ 3 = 16.

questions.s: A man bought 6 pens at a mean price of Rs 12. He then bought some more pens at a mean price of Rs 15, and the mean price over all the pens became Rs 14. How many pens did he buy in the second purchase?
questions.e: Let the second purchase be k pens. Then 72 + 15k = 14(6 + k) = 84 + 14k, so k = 12. By balancing: 14 is 2 above 12 and 1 below 15, so the pens are in the ratio 1 : 2 for the two prices, i.e. 6 : 12.

questions.s: The average of 6 numbers is 28. Each of the first three is increased by 6 and each of the last three is decreased by 4. What is the new average?
questions.e: Total change = 3 × 6 − 3 × 4 = +6, so the total rises from 168 to 174 and the mean from 28 to 29. Ignoring the decrease on the last three would give 28 + 3 = 31.

questions.s: The average of the ages of a father and his son is 28 years. The father is three times as old as the son. How old will the father be in 6 years' time?
questions.e: Together they are 2 × 28 = 56 years old. With the father three times the son, the ages are 14 and 42 (3x + x = 56, x = 14). In 6 years the father will be 48. The value 42 is his age now.

questions.s: The maximum temperatures in Lahore over five days were 31, 33, 30, 34 and 32 °C. What was the mean maximum temperature?
questions.e: Sum = 160 and 160 ÷ 5 = 32 °C. The sum is not a temperature, and 33 is only the second reading.

questions.s: What is the mean of the first 10 even natural numbers?
questions.e: The numbers are 2, 4, ..., 20 with sum 110, so the mean is 110 ÷ 10 = 11. It lies midway between the first (2) and last (20) values, not at 10.

questions.s: The average of four numbers is 12.5. What is their sum?
questions.e: Sum = average × count = 12.5 × 4 = 50. Dividing 12.5 by 4 gives 3.125 and goes the wrong way.

questions.s: What is the mean of 0.2, 0.5 and 0.8?
questions.e: Sum = 1.5 and 1.5 ÷ 3 = 0.5. The sum 1.5 has not been divided by the number of values.

questions.s: Ali buys four notebooks costing Rs 40, Rs 55, Rs 60 and Rs 45. What is the average price of a notebook?
questions.e: Total cost = 40 + 55 + 60 + 45 = 200, and 200 ÷ 4 = 50 rupees per notebook. Rs 200 is the total spent.

questions.s: The average of nine numbers is 22. A tenth number is added and the average becomes 23. What is the tenth number?
questions.e: New total = 10 × 23 = 230 and old total = 9 × 22 = 198, so the tenth number is 32. It has to lift each of the nine old numbers by 1 (9 more) as well as reach the new mean of 23, so 22 + 1 + 9 = 32.

questions.s: Section A has 24 students with a mean mark of 75 and section B has 36 students with a mean mark of 65. What is the mean mark of the 60 students together?
questions.e: Total = 24 × 75 + 36 × 65 = 1,800 + 2,340 = 4,140, and 4,140 ÷ 60 = 69. The simple mean of 75 and 65 is 70, but section B is larger, so the true mean is lower.

questions.s: The mean age of 8 people is 32 years. A man aged 40 leaves and a woman aged 24 joins. What is the new mean age?
questions.e: Old total = 8 × 32 = 256. After the change: 256 − 40 + 24 = 240, and 240 ÷ 8 = 30 years. The group is still 8 people, but the total fell by 16.

questions.s: The average of five numbers is 24. Two of them, 20 and 28, are removed. What is the average of the remaining three?
questions.e: Total = 5 × 24 = 120. The removed numbers sum to 48, so the rest total 72 and the mean is 72 ÷ 3 = 24. The two removed numbers are balanced around 24, so the mean does not change.

questions.s: The average of three consecutive multiples of 5 is 40. What is the smallest of them?
questions.e: The middle multiple is the mean, 40, so the three are 35, 40 and 45. Starting at 30 would make the middle number 35.

questions.s: A batsman's average after 12 innings is 35. After his 13th innings it is 37. How many runs did he score in the 13th innings?
questions.e: New total = 13 × 37 = 481 and old total = 12 × 35 = 420, so he scored 61. The 13th innings must also raise each of the earlier 12 by 2 runs, so 37 is too low.

questions.s: The mean of x and y is 9 and the mean of y and z is 11. What is z − x?
questions.e: x + y = 18 and y + z = 22. Subtracting gives z − x = 22 − 18 = 4. The means differ by 2, but the sums differ by twice that.

questions.s: The average age of 6 people is 30 years. When a seventh person joins, the average becomes 31 years. When an eighth person joins, it becomes 32 years. How old is the eighth person?
questions.e: Total of six = 180; with the seventh it is 7 × 31 = 217 (seventh aged 37); with the eighth it is 8 × 32 = 256. The eighth person is 256 − 217 = 39 years old. The figure 37 is the seventh person's age.

questions.s: The average of a, b and c is 16, where the mean of a and b is 14 and the mean of b and c is 16. What is the mean of c and a?
