questions.e: a + b + c = 48, a + b = 28 and b + c = 32. So c = 48 − 28 = 20 and a = 48 − 32 = 16, and (c + a) ÷ 2 = 18. The mean 16 is just the overall mean of all three.

questions.s: A class of 40 students has an average mark of 55. The students who passed have an average of 65 and those who failed have an average of 40. How many students passed?
questions.e: Let p passed: 65p + 40(40 − p) = 55 × 40 = 2,200, so 25p = 600 and p = 24. Check by balancing: 55 is 15 above 40 and 10 below 65, so passed : failed = 15 : 10 = 3 : 2, which is 24 : 16.

questions.s: A car travels at 60 km/h for 2.5 hours. How far does it go?
questions.e: Distance = speed × time = 60 × 2.5 = 150 km. Dividing 60 by 2.5 gives 24 and would be a time or rate, not a distance.

questions.s: Convert 72 km/h into metres per second.
questions.e: 1 km/h = 1,000 m ÷ 3,600 s = 5/18 m/s, so 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s. Multiplying by 18/5 converts in the wrong direction and gives 259.2.

questions.s: A car moves at 25 m/s. What is this in km/h?
questions.e: To change m/s into km/h multiply by 18/5: 25 × 18/5 = 90 km/h. Dividing by 3.6 would go the wrong way and give about 6.9.

questions.s: How long does a bus take to cover 240 km at 80 km/h?
questions.e: Time = distance ÷ speed = 240 ÷ 80 = 3 hours. Inverting the ratio (80 ÷ 240) gives 0.33, which is hours per kilometre, not hours.

questions.s: A bus covers 180 km in 4 hours 30 minutes. What is its average speed?
questions.e: Convert the time to 4.5 hours: 180 ÷ 4.5 = 40 km/h. Using 4 hours and ignoring the 30 minutes gives 45 km/h.

questions.s: Two men start from the same spot and walk in opposite directions at 4 km/h and 5 km/h. How far apart are they after 3 hours?
questions.e: In opposite directions the speeds add: 9 km/h × 3 h = 27 km. Subtracting the speeds (1 × 3 = 3 km) applies the same-direction rule.

questions.s: A can finish a piece of work in 10 days and B can finish it in 15 days. Working together, how many days will they take?
questions.e: In one day they do 1/10 + 1/15 = 5/30 = 1/6 of the work, so together they need 6 days. Averaging the two times (12.5) is wrong because working together must be faster than either alone.

questions.s: A pipe fills a tank in 6 hours. What fraction of the tank does it fill in 2 hours?
questions.e: The pipe fills 1/6 of the tank each hour, so in 2 hours it fills 2/6 = 1/3. The value 1/6 is only one hour's work.

questions.s: A cyclist covers 15 km at 20 km/h. How many minutes does this take?
questions.e: Time = 15 ÷ 20 = 0.75 hour, and 0.75 × 60 = 45 minutes. The value 75 results from reading 0.75 hour as 75 minutes.

questions.s: A train 200 m long passes a signal pole at 20 m/s. How long does it take?
questions.e: To pass a pole the train covers its own length: 200 ÷ 20 = 10 seconds. Doubling the length for a pole (40 s) is not needed; that is for a platform of equal length.

questions.s: 8 workers build a wall in 12 days. How many workers are needed to build it in 6 days?
questions.e: Total work = 8 × 12 = 96 worker-days. In 6 days we need 96 ÷ 6 = 16 workers. Halving the time doubles the workers, so 4 (halved) has the proportion the wrong way round.

questions.s: 5 men dig a trench in 18 days. Working at the same rate, how many days would 6 men need?
questions.e: Total work = 5 × 18 = 90 man-days. With 6 men the time is 90 ÷ 6 = 15 days. More men mean fewer days, so 21.6 (which multiplies by 6/5) is the wrong direction.

questions.s: Imran walks at 5 km/h for 36 minutes. How far does he walk?
questions.e: 36 minutes = 0.6 hour, so distance = 5 × 0.6 = 3 km. Multiplying 5 by 36 without converting the minutes gives 180.

questions.s: Two cars travel in the same direction on a straight road at 70 km/h and 55 km/h. At what rate does the gap between them change?
questions.e: In the same direction the relative speed is the difference: 70 − 55 = 15 km/h. 125 km/h is the sum, which applies when they move towards or away from each other in opposite directions.

questions.s: A runner covers 100 m in 20 seconds at a steady pace. What is his speed in km/h?
questions.e: Speed = 100 ÷ 20 = 5 m/s, and 5 × 18/5 = 18 km/h. The value 5 is the speed but still in m/s.

questions.s: A car goes 45 km in 1 hour 30 minutes. At the same speed, how far does it travel in 4 hours?
questions.e: Speed = 45 ÷ 1.5 = 30 km/h, so in 4 hours it covers 120 km. Taking 45 km per hour gives 180 km.

questions.s: A can complete a job in 8 days working alone. What fraction of the job does he complete in 3 days?
questions.e: A does 1/8 of the job each day, so in 3 days he does 3/8. The fraction 5/8 is what is left, not what is done.

questions.s: A journey is 150 km long. After covering 2/5 of it, how many kilometres are left?
questions.e: 2/5 of 150 = 60 km has been covered, so 150 − 60 = 90 km remain. The value 60 is the distance already covered.

questions.s: A train 120 m long travelling at 54 km/h meets a train 180 m long travelling at 36 km/h in the opposite direction on a parallel track. How long do they take to cross each other completely?
questions.e: Speeds in m/s are 15 and 10. In opposite directions they add: 25 m/s. Distance to clear = 120 + 180 = 300 m, so time = 300 ÷ 25 = 12 s. Subtracting the speeds (5 m/s) gives 60 s and treats them as moving in the same direction.

questions.s: A train 150 m long crosses a 250 m platform in 20 seconds. What is its speed?
questions.e: Distance covered = 150 + 250 = 400 m in 20 s, so 20 m/s = 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h. Using only 250 m gives 45 km/h and ignores the train's own length.

questions.s: A boat goes 12 km/h in still water and the stream flows at 3 km/h. How long does it take to travel 45 km downstream?
questions.e: Downstream speed = 12 + 3 = 15 km/h, so time = 45 ÷ 15 = 3 hours. 5 hours uses the upstream speed (9 km/h) and 3.75 hours ignores the stream.

questions.s: A boat travels downstream at 18 km/h and upstream at 10 km/h. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.e: Stream speed = (downstream − upstream) ÷ 2 = (18 − 10) ÷ 2 = 4 km/h. The value 14 is the boat's speed in still water, (18 + 10) ÷ 2.

questions.s: A can do a piece of work in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work together for 4 days and then A leaves. How many more days will B need to finish the work?
questions.e: Together they do 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 per day, so in 4 days they do 20/36 = 5/9. Remaining 4/9 at B's rate 1/18 takes (4/9) × 18 = 8 days. Taking 6 days ignores that B is slower than the pair.

questions.s: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and pipe B can empty it in 20 hours. If both are opened together with the tank empty, how long will it take to fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/12 − 1/20 = (5 − 3)/60 = 1/30 of the tank per hour, so it takes 30 hours. 7.5 hours treats both pipes as filling.

questions.s: A car travels from Lahore to a city at 50 km/h and returns along the same road at 75 km/h. What is its average speed for the round trip?
questions.e: Equal distances at two speeds: average = 2 × 50 × 75 ÷ (50 + 75) = 7,500 ÷ 125 = 60 km/h. The simple mean 62.5 would need equal times at each speed.

questions.s: Two cities are 360 km apart. Two cars leave them at the same time and drive towards each other at 50 km/h and 70 km/h. After how many hours do they meet?
questions.e: Closing speed = 50 + 70 = 120 km/h, so they meet after 360 ÷ 120 = 3 hours. The value 7.2 hours is the time the slower car alone would take for the whole 360 km.

questions.s: A boat's speed in still water is 10 km/h and the stream flows at 2 km/h. How long does it take to go 12 km upstream and come back the same 12 km?
questions.e: Upstream speed is 8 km/h, so 12 km takes 1.5 h; downstream speed is 12 km/h, so it takes 1 h. Total = 2.5 hours. Using the still-water speed for the whole 24 km gives 2.4 hours.

questions.s: A can finish a job in 15 days and B in 10 days. They work together for 3 days and then A leaves. How many days will B need to finish the rest?
questions.e: Together they do 1/15 + 1/10 = 1/6 per day, so in 3 days they do 1/2 of the job. B does the remaining half alone at 1/10 per day: 5 days.

questions.s: A worker and a helper are paid Rs 4,500 in total for a job on which they work together. The worker alone could finish in 6 days and the helper alone in 12 days. What is the worker's share, if pay is in proportion to work done?
questions.e: Their daily rates are 1/6 and 1/12, a ratio of 2 : 1. The worker's share is 2/3 of 4,500 = Rs 3,000. Splitting equally (Rs 2,250) ignores that the worker does twice as much.

questions.s: Two pipes can fill a cistern in 20 minutes and 30 minutes respectively. How long will they take to fill it if both are open?
questions.e: The pipes fill 1/20 + 1/30 = 5/60 = 1/12 of the cistern per minute, so the time is 12 minutes. Averaging the times (25) ignores that they work together.

questions.s: Walking at 4/5 of his usual speed, a man reaches his office 15 minutes later than usual. What is his usual time for the journey?
questions.e: At 4/5 of the speed the time is 5/4 of the usual time, so the extra 1/4 of the usual time is 15 minutes. Usual time = 4 × 15 = 60 minutes. Taking 15 minutes as 1/5 of the usual time would give 75.

questions.s: Two runners start at the same point on a circular track of 400 m and run in the same direction at 6 m/s and 4 m/s. After how many seconds does the faster runner first lap the slower?
questions.e: The faster runner gains 6 − 4 = 2 m/s and must gain one full lap of 400 m: 400 ÷ 2 = 200 s. Adding the speeds would give 400 ÷ 10 = 40 s, the time to meet if they ran in opposite directions.

questions.s: A coach travels 380 km: the first 190 km at 76 km/h and the remaining 190 km at 95 km/h. How long does the journey take?
questions.e: First part: 190 ÷ 76 = 2.5 h. Second part: 190 ÷ 95 = 2 h. Total = 4.5 h = 4 h 30 min. Using the simple mean speed 85.5 km/h gives about 4 h 27 min, which is wrong because the times are unequal.

questions.s: Ahmed can do a job in 12 days. His brother is twice as fast. Working together, how many days do they need?
questions.e: The brother needs 6 days alone. Together: 1/12 + 1/6 = 3/12 = 1/4 per day, so 4 days. Saying 6 days takes only the brother's time, forgetting Ahmed's help.

questions.s: The ratio of the speeds of two cars is 3 : 4. What is the ratio of the times they take to cover the same distance?
questions.e: For a fixed distance, time is inversely proportional to speed, so the ratio of times is the reverse: 4 : 3. Keeping 3 : 4 treats time as directly proportional to speed.

questions.s: 12 workers build 3 identical walls in 18 days. How many days would 15 workers take to build 5 such walls?
questions.e: One wall needs 12 × 18 ÷ 3 = 72 worker-days, so 5 walls need 360. With 15 workers: 360 ÷ 15 = 24 days. Scaling only the workers or only the walls misses the combined effect.

questions.s: A walks to school at 4 km/h and reaches 10 minutes late. At 5 km/h he reaches 8 minutes early. What is the distance to school?
questions.e: The two journeys differ by 18 minutes = 0.3 hour. d/4 − d/5 = d/20 = 0.3, so d = 6 km. Taking the time difference as 2 minutes (10 − 8) misses that one trip is late and the other is early.

questions.s: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 and 30 minutes respectively, and pipe C can empty the full tank in 60 minutes. If all three are opened together, how long does the empty tank take to fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/20 + 1/30 − 1/60 = (3 + 2 − 1)/60 = 4/60 = 1/15, so the tank fills in 15 minutes. Treating C as an inlet gives 10 minutes; ignoring it gives 12.

questions.s: A can do a job in 12 days. B is 50% more efficient than A. How many days does B take to do the same job?
questions.e: B's rate is 1.5 times A's, so B's time is 12 ÷ 1.5 = 8 days. Adding 50% to the time instead gives 18 days, which would make B slower.

questions.s: A car travels 150 km at 50 km/h and then 50 km at 25 km/h. What is its average speed over the 200 km?
questions.e: Time = 150 ÷ 50 + 50 ÷ 25 = 3 + 2 = 5 hours, so the average speed is 200 ÷ 5 = 40 km/h. The mean of the speeds is 37.5, which ignores that more distance was covered at the higher speed.

questions.s: A train takes 6 hours to cover a distance at 50 km/h. At what speed must it run to cover the same distance in 5 hours?
questions.e: Distance = 50 × 6 = 300 km, so the speed needed is 300 ÷ 5 = 60 km/h. Adding 1 hour's worth of speed per hour saved (55) does not reflect the inverse relation between speed and time.

questions.s: How far does a car travelling at 54 km/h move in 12 seconds?
questions.e: 54 km/h = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s, so in 12 s it covers 15 × 12 = 180 m. Multiplying 54 by 12 gives 648 and mixes km/h with seconds.

questions.s: A and B together can finish a job in 8 days. A alone can finish it in 12 days. How many days would B alone take?
questions.e: B's daily rate = 1/8 − 1/12 = 1/24, so B alone needs 24 days. Subtracting the times (12 − 8 = 4) is not valid for rates.

questions.s: A 600-litre tank is filled by a tap at 12 litres per minute, while a leak drains 2 litres per minute. How long does the tank take to fill from empty?
questions.e: The net filling rate is 12 − 2 = 10 litres per minute, so 600 ÷ 10 = 60 minutes. 50 minutes ignores the leak, and 75 reverses it.

questions.s: A worker completes 3/4 of a job in 9 days. At the same rate, how many more days does he need to finish the job?
questions.e: He does 3/4 in 9 days, so 1/4 takes 9 ÷ 3 = 3 days. The value 12 is the time for the whole job.

questions.s: Two people start from the same point and walk in opposite directions at 5 km/h and 7 km/h. After how many hours will they be 30 km apart?
questions.e: They separate at 5 + 7 = 12 km/h, so the time is 30 ÷ 12 = 2.5 hours. Using their difference, 2 km/h, would give 15 hours, which is the same-direction rule.

questions.s: A 100 m long train passes a man walking in the same direction as the train at 6 km/h in 10 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.e: Relative speed = 100 ÷ 10 = 10 m/s = 36 km/h. Since the man moves with the train, relative speed = train − 6, so the train goes 42 km/h. 36 forgets the man's speed; 30 subtracts it instead.

questions.s: A leaves a town at 06:00 driving at 40 km/h. At 08:00 B leaves the same town on the same road at 60 km/h. At what time does B overtake A?
questions.e: By 08:00 A is 80 km ahead. B gains 60 − 40 = 20 km/h, so B needs 80 ÷ 20 = 4 hours: 12:00. Dividing the 80 km lead by A's own speed gives 2 hours, i.e. 10:00, but that ignores that B is much faster than A.

questions.s: A pump fills a tank in 6 hours. Because of a leak, it takes 8 hours to fill the tank. How long would the leak alone take to empty a full tank?
questions.e: The leak's rate = 1/6 − 1/8 = (4 − 3)/24 = 1/24 of the tank per hour, so it empties a full tank in 24 hours. Subtracting the times (8 − 6 = 2) is invalid for rates.

questions.s: A 240 m long train moving at 90 km/h crosses a bridge 260 m long. How many seconds does it take from the engine entering to the last coach leaving the bridge?
questions.e: 90 km/h = 25 m/s and the distance covered is 240 + 260 = 500 m, so the time is 500 ÷ 25 = 20 s. Using 240 m gives 9.6 s and using 260 m gives 10.4 s, each ignoring part of the distance.

questions.s: A, B and C together can finish a job in 4 days. A and B together need 6 days. How many days does C alone need?
questions.e: C's rate = 1/4 − 1/6 = 1/12 per day, so C alone needs 12 days. The difference in the days (6 − 4 = 2) is not the time for C.

questions.s: A and B together can complete a task in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, and A and C in 20 days. How many days will all three take working together?
questions.e: Adding the three pair rates gives 2(A + B + C) = 1/12 + 1/15 + 1/20 = 12/60 = 1/5, so A + B + C = 1/10 per day and the answer is 10 days. Forgetting to halve the sum gives 5 days.

questions.s: A pipe fills a tank in 8 hours and a second pipe empties it in 24 hours. Both are opened together on the empty tank. After 4 hours the emptying pipe is closed. How much longer does the tank take to fill?
questions.e: Net rate with both open = 1/8 − 1/24 = 1/12, so in 4 hours 1/3 is filled. The remaining 2/3 at 1/8 per hour takes (2/3) × 8 = 16/3 hours = 5 h 20 min. The 4 hours already spent is not the time still needed.

questions.s: A train takes 18 seconds to pass a pole and 30 seconds to cross a platform 240 m long, at a constant speed. What is the length of the train?
questions.e: The extra 30 − 18 = 12 s is the time to cover the platform's 240 m, so the speed is 20 m/s. In 18 s the train covers its own length: 20 × 18 = 360 m. The platform length 240 m is not the train length.

questions.s: A boat takes 2 hours longer to go 24 km upstream than 24 km downstream. If the stream flows at 3 km/h, what is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.e: Let the boat speed be b. 24/(b − 3) − 24/(b + 3) = 2 gives 24 × 6 = 2(b² − 9), so b² = 81 and b = 9. Check: upstream 6 km/h takes 4 h and downstream 12 km/h takes 2 h, a difference of 2 h; 12 km/h is the downstream speed in the check, not the boat's own speed.

questions.s: A can do a job in 20 days and B in 30 days. They start working together, but A leaves 5 days before the job is finished. In how many days is the job completed?
questions.e: Let the total time be T days. B works all T days and A works T − 5 days: (T − 5)/20 + T/30 = 1. Multiplying by 60: 3(T − 5) + 2T = 60, so T = 15. Treating the last 5 days as shared would give 12.

questions.s: 10 men complete one-third of a job in 8 days. How many more men must be added so that the rest of the job is finished in the next 8 days?
questions.e: One-third of the job in 8 days means 10 men do 1/3 per 8 days. The remaining 2/3 in 8 days needs twice as many workers: 20 men, so 10 more must be added. The value 20 is the total, not the number added.

questions.s: The speed of a car is increased by 25%. By what percentage does the time taken for the same journey decrease?
questions.e: New speed = 1.25 × old, so new time = 1/1.25 = 0.8 of the old time, a decrease of 20%. A 25% decrease would assume that time and speed change by equal percentages, but they are inversely related.

questions.s: Train A leaves station X at 08:00 at 60 km/h towards station Y, 300 km away. Train B leaves Y at 09:00 at 40 km/h towards X. At what time do the trains meet?
questions.e: By 09:00 train A has covered 60 km, leaving 240 km. The trains close at 60 + 40 = 100 km/h, so they meet after 2.4 hours (2 h 24 min): 11:24. Ignoring B's later start gives 300 ÷ 100 = 3 hours from 08:00, which is 11:00.

questions.s: Two trains, 150 m and 100 m long, run on parallel tracks in the same direction at 60 km/h and 45 km/h. How long does the faster train take to completely pass the slower one?
questions.e: Relative speed = 15 km/h = 15 × 5/18 = 25/6 m/s. Distance to clear = 150 + 100 = 250 m, so time = 250 ÷ (25/6) = 60 s. Using only the faster train's length gives 36 s.

questions.s: Convert 90 km/h into metres per second.
questions.e: Multiply by 5/18: 90 × 5/18 = 25 m/s. Multiplying by 18/5 would give 324.

questions.s: How long does a train take to cover 210 km at 35 km/h?
questions.e: Time = 210 ÷ 35 = 6 hours. Multiplying the two numbers (7,350) combines distance and speed incorrectly.

questions.s: Ahmed walks 1.5 km in 20 minutes. What is his speed in km/h?
questions.e: 20 minutes = 1/3 hour, so speed = 1.5 × 3 = 4.5 km/h. Multiplying 1.5 by 20 gives 30, forgetting to convert minutes to hours.

questions.s: 9 men finish a job in 8 days. How many days will 6 men take at the same rate?
questions.e: Total work = 9 × 8 = 72 man-days, so 6 men need 72 ÷ 6 = 12 days. Fewer men take longer, so 5.3 days (which scales the wrong way) cannot be right.

questions.s: A tap fills a tank in 40 minutes. What fraction of the tank does it fill in 10 minutes?
questions.e: In 10 minutes it fills 10/40 = 1/4 of the tank. The value 1/10 is the 10 minutes read as a fraction of 100.

questions.s: A 90 m train and a 110 m train run towards each other on parallel tracks at 60 km/h and 40 km/h. How many seconds do they take to cross each other completely?
questions.e: Closing speed = 100 km/h = 250/9 m/s. Distance = 90 + 110 = 200 m, so time = 200 × 9/250 = 7.2 s. Using the difference of speeds (20 km/h) gives 36 s, which applies to trains moving the same way.

questions.s: A boat moves at 15 km/h in still water and the stream flows at 5 km/h. How long does it take to go 40 km upstream and then 40 km back downstream?
questions.e: Upstream speed = 10 km/h, so 40 km takes 4 h; downstream speed = 20 km/h, so 40 km takes 2 h. Total = 6 hours. Using the stream speed of 5 km/h for one leg (8 hours) ignores the boat's own speed.

questions.s: A can finish a job in 14 days and B in 21 days. How long will they take working together?
questions.e: Combined rate = 1/14 + 1/21 = (3 + 2)/42 = 5/42 per day, so the time is 42/5 = 8.4 days. The mean of the two times (17.5) is longer than either person's own time would allow together.

questions.s: A and B together can do a job in 10 days. A alone can do it in 15 days. How many days does B alone need?
questions.e: B's rate = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30, so B alone needs 30 days. Subtracting the days (15 − 10 = 5) is invalid for rates.

questions.s: Two trains start from stations 280 km apart and travel towards each other at 30 km/h and 40 km/h. After how many hours do they meet?
questions.e: They close the gap at 30 + 40 = 70 km/h, so they meet after 280 ÷ 70 = 4 hours. The value 7 is 280 ÷ 40, the time the faster train alone would need for the whole distance.

questions.s: A driver going at 40 km/h arrives 12 minutes late. Going at 50 km/h, he would arrive 6 minutes early. How long is the journey?
questions.e: The time difference is 12 + 6 = 18 minutes = 0.3 hour. d/40 − d/50 = d/200 = 0.3, so d = 60 km.

questions.s: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours and pipe B fills it in 9 hours. How long will both together take?
questions.e: Combined rate = 1/6 + 1/9 = 5/18 per hour, so time = 18/5 = 3.6 hours = 3 h 36 min. The sum of the times (15 hours) divided by two gives 7.5 hours, which is longer than either pipe alone.

questions.s: A can do a job in 12 days, B in 24 days and C in 8 days. A and B start; C joins them after 2 days. In how many days in all is the job completed?
questions.e: A and B together do 1/12 + 1/24 = 1/8 per day, so 2 days give 1/4. With C, the combined rate is 1/8 + 1/8 = 1/4, so the remaining 3/4 takes 3 days. Total = 5 days. Forgetting the first 2 days gives 3, and ignoring C gives 8.

questions.s: A starts cycling at 30 km/h along a road. Two hours later B leaves the same point and follows at 50 km/h. How far from the start does B overtake A?
questions.e: A has a 60 km lead. B gains 50 − 30 = 20 km/h, so B needs 3 hours and covers 50 × 3 = 150 km. The value 90 is the distance A walks in those three hours, not where they meet.

questions.s: The speed of a bus is reduced by 20%. By what percentage does the time for the same journey increase?
questions.e: New speed = 0.8 × old, so the new time = 1/0.8 = 1.25 of the old, an increase of 25%. A 20% increase assumes the percentages are equal, but time is inversely proportional to speed.

questions.s: A shopkeeper buys an article for Rs 800 and sells it for Rs 920. What is his profit percentage?
questions.e: Profit = 920 − 800 = Rs 120, and profit % = 120 ÷ 800 × 100 = 15%. Profit is always taken on the cost price; dividing by 920 would give about 13%.

questions.s: A radio bought for Rs 500 is sold for Rs 450. What is the loss percentage?
questions.e: Loss = Rs 50 and loss % = 50 ÷ 500 × 100 = 10%. Dividing by the selling price (450) gives 11.11%, but percentages are based on the cost price.

questions.s: The marked price of a bag is Rs 2,000 and a discount of 15% is given. What is the selling price?
questions.e: Discount = 15% of 2,000 = Rs 300, so the selling price is 2,000 − 300 = Rs 1,700. Rs 300 is the discount itself, not the price paid.

questions.s: What is the simple interest on Rs 5,000 at 8% per annum for 3 years?
questions.e: SI = P × R × T ÷ 100 = 5,000 × 8 × 3 ÷ 100 = Rs 1,200. Rs 400 is only one year's interest, and Rs 6,200 is the amount, not the interest.

questions.s: Rs 4,000 is lent at 5% simple interest per annum for 2 years. What is the total amount to be repaid?
questions.e: SI = 4,000 × 5 × 2 ÷ 100 = Rs 400, so the amount = 4,000 + 400 = Rs 4,400. Rs 400 is the interest only, and Rs 4,200 counts just one year of interest.

questions.s: A shopkeeper buys 12 pens for Rs 240 and sells each pen for Rs 25. What is his profit percentage?
questions.e: Cost per pen = 240 ÷ 12 = Rs 20, so profit per pen = Rs 5 and profit % = 5 ÷ 20 × 100 = 25%. The value 5 is the profit in rupees, not the percentage.

questions.s: What is the selling price of an article whose cost price is Rs 600 if it is sold at a profit of 20%?
questions.e: Profit = 20% of 600 = Rs 120, so SP = 600 + 120 = Rs 720. Rs 480 is the selling price at a 20% loss.

questions.s: A table costing Rs 1,500 is sold at a loss of 10%. What is its selling price?
questions.e: Loss = 10% of 1,500 = Rs 150, so SP = 1,500 − 150 = Rs 1,350. Rs 1,650 would be the price at a 10% profit.

questions.s: The marked price of a shirt is Rs 500 and it is sold for Rs 400. What is the percentage discount?
questions.e: Discount = Rs 100 and discount % = 100 ÷ 500 × 100 = 20%. Discount is calculated on the marked price, not the selling price (which would give 25%).

questions.s: What is the simple interest on Rs 6,000 at 5% per annum for 2 years?
questions.e: SI = 6,000 × 5 × 2 ÷ 100 = Rs 600. Rs 300 is one year's interest and Rs 6,600 includes the principal.

questions.s: A sum of Rs 3,000 earns simple interest of Rs 360 in 2 years. What is the rate per annum?
questions.e: Rate = SI × 100 ÷ (P × T) = 360 × 100 ÷ (3,000 × 2) = 6%. The value 12% results from forgetting to divide by the 2 years.

questions.s: In how many years will Rs 2,000 earn simple interest of Rs 400 at 10% per annum?
questions.e: Time = SI × 100 ÷ (P × R) = 400 × 100 ÷ (2,000 × 10) = 2 years. One year's interest at 10% is Rs 200, so Rs 400 needs two years.

questions.s: A shop gives successive discounts of 20% and 10% on a jacket marked at Rs 2,500. What is the price paid?
questions.e: After 20% off: 2,500 × 0.80 = 2,000. After a further 10%: 2,000 × 0.90 = Rs 1,800. A single 30% discount (Rs 1,750) is wrong because the second discount applies to the reduced price.

questions.s: An article is sold for Rs 1,260 at a profit of 5%. What was its cost price?
questions.e: SP = 1.05 × CP, so CP = 1,260 ÷ 1.05 = Rs 1,200. Taking 5% of the selling price (Rs 63) gives 1,197 but the profit is 5% of the cost.

questions.s: A man sells a bicycle for Rs 4,400 at a loss of 12%. What did the bicycle cost him?
questions.e: SP = 0.88 × CP, so CP = 4,400 ÷ 0.88 = Rs 5,000. Multiplying 4,400 by 1.12 gives 4,928, which takes 12% of the selling price.

questions.s: A dealer sells two items at Rs 1,200 each. On one he makes a profit of 20% and on the other a loss of 20%. What is the overall result?
questions.e: The first cost 1,200 ÷ 1.2 = Rs 1,000 and the second cost 1,200 ÷ 0.8 = Rs 1,500. Total cost is Rs 2,500 against total sales of Rs 2,400, a loss of Rs 100. Equal percentages do not cancel because they apply to different costs.

questions.s: What is the compound interest on Rs 10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
questions.e: Amount = 10,000 × 1.1² = 12,100, so CI = 12,100 − 10,000 = Rs 2,100. Rs 2,000 is the simple interest, and Rs 12,100 is the amount.

questions.s: What is the difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on Rs 5,000 at 8% per annum for 2 years?
A trader marks his goods 25% above the cost price and then allows a discount of 10%. What is his profit percentage?
questions.e: Take CP = 100. Marked price = 125 and SP = 125 × 0.9 = 112.5, so the profit is 12.5%. Subtracting the percentages (25 − 10 = 15) is wrong because the discount applies to the marked price.

questions.s: A vendor buys 15 oranges for Rs 60 and sells 12 oranges for Rs 60. What is his gain percentage?
questions.e: Cost per orange = 60 ÷ 15 = Rs 4 and selling price per orange = 60 ÷ 12 = Rs 5, so the gain is 1 ÷ 4 = 25%. Using the difference in numbers (3) over 15 gives 20%.

questions.s: An article sold for Rs 1,150 gives a profit of 15%. At what price should it be sold to incur a loss of 5%?
questions.e: CP = 1,150 ÷ 1.15 = Rs 1,000. A 5% loss gives SP = 1,000 × 0.95 = Rs 950. Subtracting 5% from 1,150 would apply the loss to the wrong base.

questions.s: A sum of Rs 8,000 becomes Rs 9,600 in 4 years at simple interest. What is the rate per annum?
questions.e: SI = 9,600 − 8,000 = Rs 1,600, so rate = 1,600 × 100 ÷ (8,000 × 4) = 5%. The 20% figure is the total over 4 years and has not been divided by the time.

questions.s: What principal earns simple interest of Rs 900 in 3 years at 6% per annum?
questions.e: P = SI × 100 ÷ (R × T) = 900 × 100 ÷ (6 × 3) = Rs 5,000. Rs 16,200 comes from multiplying by 18 instead of dividing.

questions.s: Two successive discounts of 10% and 10% are equal to a single discount of what percentage?
questions.e: Price after both = 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.81 of the marked price, so the single discount is 19%. Adding the discounts (20%) ignores that the second applies to the lowered price.

questions.s: A school bag with cost price Rs 400 is marked up by 40% and then sold after a discount of 25%. What is the selling price?
questions.e: Marked price = 400 × 1.4 = Rs 560 and SP = 560 × 0.75 = Rs 420. A net 15% gain (Rs 460) subtracts the percentages directly, which is wrong.

questions.s: A sells an article to B at a profit of 20%, and B sells it to C at a profit of 10% for Rs 1,980. What did A pay for the article?
questions.e: B paid 1,980 ÷ 1.10 = Rs 1,800, and A's cost was 1,800 ÷ 1.20 = Rs 1,500. Rs 1,800 is only B's cost, and 1,386 takes 30% off the final price.

questions.s: What is the amount on Rs 8,000 at 5% per annum compounded annually for 2 years?
questions.e: Amount = 8,000 × 1.05² = 8,000 × 1.1025 = Rs 8,820. Rs 8,800 is the amount at simple interest (8,000 + 800), and Rs 8,400 adds only one year's interest.

questions.s: A shopkeeper finds that the cost price of 10 articles equals the selling price of 8 articles. What is his profit percentage?
questions.e: Let each article cost Rs 1. Then 8 articles are sold for Rs 10, so SP per article = 1.25 and profit = 25%. The 20% figure is 2 ÷ 10 and uses the wrong base.

questions.s: Zainab invests Rs 6,000 at 10% simple interest and Rs 4,000 at 12% simple interest per annum. What is her total interest after 2 years?
questions.e: Interest on the first sum = 6,000 × 10 × 2 ÷ 100 = Rs 1,200. On the second = 4,000 × 12 × 2 ÷ 100 = Rs 960. Total = Rs 2,160. Applying the average rate 11% to Rs 10,000 gives 2,200, which ignores the unequal amounts.

questions.s: A shopkeeper gives a 20% discount on the marked price and still makes a 10% profit. If the cost price is Rs 880, what is the marked price?
questions.e: SP = 880 × 1.10 = Rs 968. Since SP = 0.8 × MP, MP = 968 ÷ 0.8 = Rs 1,210. Adding 25% to cost (Rs 1,100) ignores the extra profit, and 1,056 deducts 20% rather than dividing.

questions.s: At simple interest a sum doubles itself in 8 years. What is the rate per annum?
questions.e: The interest equals the principal in 8 years, so 8 × R = 100, giving R = 12.5% per annum. Dividing 100 by 12 or by 10 changes the time.

questions.s: A fruit seller buys 100 kg of mangoes at Rs 120 per kg. 10 kg are spoilt and discarded. At what price per kg must he sell the rest to gain 20% on his total cost?
questions.e: Total cost = 100 × 120 = Rs 12,000. For a 20% gain he needs Rs 14,400 from 90 kg, so the price is 14,400 ÷ 90 = Rs 160 per kg. Rs 144 is a 20% mark-up on 120, which forgets the spoilt fruit.

questions.s: Rs 12,000 is invested at 10% per annum compound interest, compounded annually. What is the amount after 3 years?
questions.e: Amount = 12,000 × 1.1³ = 12,000 × 1.331 = Rs 15,972. Rs 15,600 is the simple-interest amount, and Rs 14,520 is the amount after only two years.

questions.s: A sum of money at compound interest amounts to Rs 5,500 after 1 year and Rs 6,050 after 2 years. What is the principal?
questions.e: The ratio 6,050 ÷ 5,500 = 1.1, so the rate is 10% per year. Principal = 5,500 ÷ 1.1 = Rs 5,000. Rs 5,500 is the amount after the first year, not the principal.

questions.s: Two successive discounts of 20% and x% together equal a single discount of 28%. What is x?
questions.e: After both discounts the price is 72% of the marked price: 0.8 × (1 − x/100) = 0.72, so 1 − x/100 = 0.9 and x = 10. The value 8 comes from 28 − 20, which ignores that the second discount works on the reduced price.

questions.s: A man sold an article for Rs 720 at a loss of 10%. At what price should he have sold it to gain 10%?
questions.e: 720 is 90% of CP, so CP = 720 ÷ 0.9 = Rs 800. For a 10% gain SP = 800 × 1.1 = Rs 880. Rs 792 adds 10% to 720, which is not the cost price.

questions.s: A trader sells at a profit of 20% after allowing a discount of 10% on the marked price. By what percentage is the marked price above the cost price?
questions.e: Let CP = 100, so SP = 120. Since SP = 0.9 × MP, MP = 120 ÷ 0.9 = 133.3, which is 33⅓% above cost. Adding the percentages (20 + 10 = 30) is wrong because the discount applies to the marked price.

questions.s: Rs 4,000 is invested at 20% per annum compounded half-yearly for 1 year. How much interest is earned?
questions.e: The rate per half-year is 10%, with 2 periods. Amount = 4,000 × 1.1² = Rs 4,840, so the interest = Rs 840. Rs 800 is the interest with only one compounding at 20%; the extra Rs 40 is interest earned on the first half-year's interest.

questions.s: Two equal sums are lent for 4 years at simple interest, one at 6% and the other at 8% per annum. The second earns Rs 480 more interest than the first. What is each sum?
questions.e: Extra interest = 2% of P per year × 4 years = 8% of P = Rs 480, so P = 480 ÷ 0.08 = Rs 6,000. Rs 24,000 comes from using 2% alone and forgetting the 4 years.

questions.s: A merchant buys two articles for Rs 1,000 in total. He sells the first at a 10% profit and the second at a 10% loss and receives Rs 1,020 in all. What did the first article cost?
questions.e: Let the first cost x. Then 1.1x + 0.9(1,000 − x) = 1,020, so 0.2x + 900 = 1,020 and x = 600. If the two costs were equal (Rs 500 each) the sales would total exactly Rs 1,000.

questions.s: An article bought for Rs 250 is sold for Rs 300. What is the profit percentage?
questions.e: Profit = Rs 50, so profit % = 50 ÷ 250 × 100 = 20%. Dividing by the selling price gives 16.7%, but profit is measured against the cost.

questions.s: A clock costing Rs 2,000 is sold at a loss of 5%. What is the selling price?
questions.e: Loss = 5% of 2,000 = Rs 100, so SP = 2,000 − 100 = Rs 1,900. Rs 2,100 would be the price at a 5% profit.

questions.s: A jacket marked at Rs 1,200 is sold at a discount of 25%. What is the selling price?
questions.e: Discount = 25% of 1,200 = Rs 300, so SP = 1,200 − 300 = Rs 900. Rs 300 is the discount, and Rs 1,500 adds it instead of subtracting.

questions.s: What is the simple interest on Rs 2,500 at 6% per annum for 4 years?
questions.e: SI = 2,500 × 6 × 4 ÷ 100 = Rs 600. Rs 150 is just one year's interest and Rs 3,100 is the amount.

questions.s: What is the amount if Rs 7,500 is lent at 4% simple interest per annum for 5 years?
questions.e: SI = 7,500 × 4 × 5 ÷ 100 = Rs 1,500, so the amount is 7,500 + 1,500 = Rs 9,000. Rs 1,500 alone is the interest.

questions.s: A radio costing Rs 2,500 is marked up by 40% and then sold at a discount of 10%. What is its selling price?
questions.e: Marked price = 2,500 × 1.4 = Rs 3,500 and SP = 3,500 × 0.9 = Rs 3,150. Rs 3,250 would take a net mark-up of 30%, which is not how successive changes combine.

questions.s: What is the compound interest on Rs 4,000 at 5% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
questions.e: Amount = 4,000 × 1.05² = 4,000 × 1.1025 = Rs 4,410, so CI = Rs 410. Rs 400 is simple interest and Rs 4,410 is the amount.

questions.s: An article is sold for Rs 1,053 at a profit of 17%. What was its cost price?
questions.e: CP = 1,053 ÷ 1.17 = Rs 900. Multiplying by 1.17 gives 1,232, and subtracting 17% of 1,053 gives about 874, both wrong bases.

questions.s: A trader sells 25 pencils for the amount he paid for 30. What is his gain percentage?
questions.e: Let each pencil cost Rs 1. Then 25 pencils are sold for Rs 30, so each sells for Rs 1.20 and the gain is 20%. The value 25% would come from comparing the 5-pencil difference with 20 instead of 25.

questions.s: Simple interest on a sum for 3 years at 5% per annum is Rs 1,200. What is the sum?
questions.e: P = SI × 100 ÷ (R × T) = 1,200 × 100 ÷ 15 = Rs 8,000. Rs 24,000 multiplies by 15 instead of dividing.

questions.s: Successive discounts of 25% and 20% are equal to a single discount of what percentage?
questions.e: Price paid = 0.75 × 0.80 = 0.60 of the marked price, so the single discount is 40%. Adding the two (45%) ignores the second discount applying to a lower price.

questions.s: Fahad borrows Rs 9,000 at 4% simple interest per annum and repays after 2 years 6 months. How much does he repay in all?
questions.e: Time = 2.5 years, so SI = 9,000 × 4 × 2.5 ÷ 100 = Rs 900 and the total is Rs 9,900. Rs 9,720 counts only 2 full years of interest and leaves out the extra 6 months.

questions.s: A profit of 25% on the cost price is what percentage of the selling price?
questions.e: Take CP = 100, so profit = 25 and SP = 125. The profit as a percentage of SP is 25 ÷ 125 × 100 = 20%. The same amount of profit is a smaller fraction of the larger selling price.

questions.s: At simple interest, a sum of money becomes 3 times itself in 20 years. What is the rate per annum?
questions.e: The interest earned equals twice the principal, so 20 × R = 200 and R = 10%. Taking the interest as three times the principal would give 15%.

questions.s: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on a sum for 2 years at 10% per annum is Rs 50. What is the sum?
questions.e: For 2 years the difference is P × (R/100)² = P × 0.01 = 50, so P = Rs 5,000. A 10% rate does not give a difference of one-tenth of the principal.

questions.s: What is the larger root of x² − 4x − 60 = 0?
questions.e: Find two numbers with sum 4 and product −60: 10 and −6, so the equation factorises as (x − 10)(x + 6) = 0. The larger root is 10. −10 is the root with its sign reversed, a slip when reading factors such as (x − a).

questions.s: How many integers x satisfy −5 ≤ 2x + 3 < 12?
questions.e: Subtract 3 throughout, then divide by 2: −4 ≤ x < 9/2. The integers in this range number 9. 10 counts one integer too many.

questions.s: The sum of three consecutive even integers is 48. What is the smallest of them?
questions.e: Let the smallest be x. Then the numbers are x, x + 2, x + 4, so 3x + 6 = 48 and x = 14. The smallest is 14. 18 is the largest of the numbers.

questions.s: Evaluate: 32 raised to the power (3/5)
questions.e: A fractional index m/n means the nth root raised to the power m. The 5th root of 32 is 2, and 2³ = 8. 2 is only the 5th root, without applying the power 3.

questions.s: What is the larger root of x² − 13x + 12 = 0?
questions.e: Find two numbers with sum 13 and product 12: 1 and 12, so the equation factorises as (x − 1)(x − 12) = 0. The larger root is 12. −12 is the root with its sign reversed, a slip when reading factors such as (x − a).

questions.s: What is the coefficient of x in the expansion of (x − 5)²?
questions.e: (x − 5)(x − 5) = x² − 10x + 25. The coefficient of x is −5 − 5 = −10. 25 is the constant term.

questions.s: Simplify: √54 − √24
questions.e: Take out square factors: √54 = 3√6 and √24 = 2√6. So the expression is (3 − 2)√6 = √6. √30 adds or subtracts the numbers under the roots.

questions.s: Solve for x: √(x − 7) = 10
questions.e: Square both sides: x − 7 = 100, so x = 107. 17 forgets to square both sides.

questions.s: For what value of k does 4x² − 32x + k = 0 have equal roots?
questions.e: Equal roots need the discriminant b² − 4ac = 0: (−32)² − 4(4)k = 0, so k = 1,024/16 = 64. 128 uses b² ÷ 2a instead of b² ÷ 4a.

questions.s: y varies inversely as x, and y = 42 when x = 3. What is y when x = 6?
questions.e: xy is constant: 3 × 42 = 126. So y = 126/6 = 21 when x = 6. 84 treats the variation as direct.

questions.s: Noor spends 1/3 of her pocket money on books and 1/4 on snacks. She has Rs 450 left. How much did she have at first, in rupees?
questions.e: The fraction left is 1 − 1/3 − 1/4 = 5/12. So she had 450 ÷ 5/12 = Rs 1,080. 3,150 multiplies by the sum of the denominators.

questions.s: The equation |x − 10| = 12 has two solutions. What is their sum?
questions.e: x − 10 = 12 or x − 10 = −12, so x = 22 or −2. Their sum is 20. 24 is the difference of the two solutions.

questions.s: How many integers x satisfy |3x − 7| < 6?
questions.e: |3x − 7| < 6 means −6 < 3x − 7 < 6, so 1/3 < x < 13/3. The integers strictly inside this range number 4. 5 is one more than the integers actually inside the range.

questions.s: What is the nature of the roots of 2x² + 3x + 11 = 0?
questions.e: The discriminant is b² − 4ac = 3² − 4(2)(11) = −79. It is negative, so there are no real roots.

questions.s: If 8x − 23 = −55, what is the value of x?
questions.e: Move the constant across: 8x = −55 + 23 = −32. Dividing by 8 gives x = −4. −32 is 8x, the value before dividing by 8.

questions.s: Junaid and Imran together have 115 marbles. Junaid has 43 more than Imran. How many does Junaid have?
questions.e: Let Imran have x; then Junaid has x + 43. So 2x + 43 = 115, giving x = 36, and Junaid has 36 + 43 = 79. 36 is the number Imran has.

questions.s: If f(x) = 2x² − x + 6, what is the value of f(−5)?
questions.e: Substitute x = −5: 2(−5)² − (−5) + 6 = 50 + 5 + 6 = 61. 51 has a sign slip on the x term.

questions.s: Evaluate: 2 to the power 2, multiplied by 2 to the power 2, divided by 2 to the power 1
questions.e: Add indices when multiplying and subtract when dividing: 2 + 2 − 1 = 3, so the value is 2³ = 8. 32 adds the index of the divisor instead of subtracting it.

questions.s: If (x + 1) is a factor of x³ + kx² + 5x + 2, what is the value of k?
questions.e: A factor means the polynomial is zero at x = −1: (−1)³ + k(−1)² + 5(−1) + 2 = 0, so k = 4. −4 has the wrong sign.

questions.s: A taxi in Peshawar charges Rs 50 as a fixed fare plus Rs 20 for each kilometre. If the total fare is Rs 370, how many kilometres were travelled?
questions.e: Remove the fixed fare: 370 − 50 = 320. Dividing by Rs 20 per km gives 16 km.

questions.s: Simplify: x⁹ × x³ ÷ (x³)³
questions.e: (x³)³ = x⁹. So the expression is x⁹ × x³ ÷ x⁹ = x³. x⁶ treats the bracketed power as a sum of indices.

questions.s: What is the smaller root of x² − 5x + 6 = 0?
questions.e: Find two numbers with sum 5 and product 6: 2 and 3, so the equation factorises as (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0. The smaller root is 2. −2 is the root with its sign reversed, a slip when reading factors such as (x − a).

questions.s: Find the value of log₁₀ 1,000.
questions.e: 1,000 = 10³, so the logarithm to base 10 is the index 3. 100 is the number divided by the base, not the index.

questions.s: Without solving, what is the product of the roots of 2x² − 7x + 9 = 0?
questions.e: For ax² + bx + c = 0 the product of roots is c/a = 9/2. −9/2 has the wrong sign.

questions.s: If x + y = 5 and x − y = 1, what is the value of xy?
questions.e: Adding the equations gives 2x = 6, so x = 3; then y = 2. Hence xy = 3 × 2 = 6. 5 multiplies the two given sums.

questions.s: Which of the following is a solution of 3x² − 11x + 6 = 0?
questions.e: Factorise: 3x² − 11x + 6 = (x − 3)(3x − 2), so the solutions are x = 3 and x = 2/3. Substituting any of the other values does not make the left side zero.

questions.s: If 2 to the power x equals 16, what is x?
questions.e: 16 = 2⁴, so x = 4. 8 is the number divided by the base.

questions.s: The sum of five consecutive integers is 155. What is the largest of them?
questions.e: Let the smallest be x. Then the numbers are x, x + 1, x + 2, x + 3, x + 4, so 5x + 10 = 155 and x = 29. The largest is 33. 29 is the smallest of the numbers.

questions.s: Solve for x: x/4 + x/5 = 27
questions.e: Multiply by the common denominator 20: 5x + 4x = 540, so 9x = 540 and x = 60. 540 stops after multiplying both sides by 20, without combining and dividing by the x-coefficient.

questions.s: Six times a number, less 18, is equal to three times the number, plus 51. What is the number?
questions.e: Form 6x − 18 = 3x + 51. Then 3x = 69, so x = 23. 11 subtracts the constants instead of adding them.

questions.s: 5 cups and 4 plates cost Rs 469. 1 cup and 1 plate cost Rs 103. What is the price of one cup, in rupees?
questions.e: Let one cup cost x and one plate cost y: 5x + 4y = 469 and x + y = 103. Eliminating one unknown gives x = 57 and y = 46. 46 is the price of one plate.

questions.s: Solve for x: 5x + 15 = 2x + 57
questions.e: Collect x-terms on one side: 3x = 57 − 15 = 42, so x = 14. 6 comes from adding the x-terms instead of subtracting them.

questions.s: Which inequality is equivalent to 7 − 2x > −2?
questions.e: Subtract 7: −2x > −9. Dividing by −2 reverses the sign, so x < 9/2. x > 9/2 forgets to reverse the inequality when dividing by a negative number.

questions.s: If x = 3 and y = 4, what is the value of 2x² − 5xy?
questions.e: x² = 9, so 2x² = 18. xy = 12, so 5xy gives −5(12) = −60. The total is −42. 78 reverses the sign of the xy term.

questions.s: If x = −4 and y = −2, what is the value of 5x² + 5xy?
questions.e: x² = 16, so 5x² = 80. xy = 8, so 5xy gives +5(8) = 40. The total is 120. 40 reverses the sign of the xy term.

questions.s: Which inequality is equivalent to 11 − 4x > −5?
questions.e: Subtract 11: −4x > −16. Dividing by −4 reverses the sign, so x < 4. x > 4 forgets to reverse the inequality when dividing by a negative number.

questions.s: How many integers x satisfy −9 ≤ 3x + 1 < 21?
questions.e: Subtract 1 throughout, then divide by 3: −10/3 ≤ x < 20/3. The integers in this range number 10. 11 counts one integer too many.

questions.s: A father is 5 times as old as his son. The sum of their ages is 60 years. How old is the father?
questions.e: Let the son be x; the father is 5x. Then 5x + x = 60, so x = 10 and the father is 5 × 10 = 50 years. 10 is the son's age.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² − 8x − 4 = 0, what is the value of 1/α + 1/β?
questions.e: 1/α + 1/β = (α + β)/(αβ) = 8/(−4) = −2, using sum = 8 and product = −4. 2 has the wrong sign.

questions.s: Evaluate: 16 raised to the power (3/2)
questions.e: A fractional index m/n means the nth root raised to the power m. The square root of 16 is 4, and 4³ = 64. 4 is only the square root, without applying the power 3.

questions.s: Evaluate: 3 to the power 5, multiplied by 3 to the power 3, divided by 3 to the power 1
questions.e: Add indices when multiplying and subtract when dividing: 5 + 3 − 1 = 7, so the value is 3⁷ = 2,187. 6,561 uses one index too many.

questions.s: If 5x + 8 = −17, what is the value of x?
questions.e: Move the constant across: 5x = −17 − 8 = −25. Dividing by 5 gives x = −5. −25 is 5x, the value before dividing by 5.

questions.s: If a + b = 14 and ab = 45, find (a − b)².
questions.e: (a − b)² = (a + b)² − 4ab = 196 − 180 = 16. 376 adds 4ab instead of subtracting it.

questions.s: What is the coefficient of x² in the expansion of (5x + 2)(x − 2)?
questions.e: The x² term comes only from 5x × x = 5x², so the coefficient is 5. 10 multiplies by the constant a.

questions.s: What is the smallest integer x satisfying 3x − 10 > 44?
questions.e: Add 10: 3x > 54, so x > 18. The smallest integer greater than 18 is 19. 18 stops at the boundary value, which does not satisfy a strict inequality.

questions.s: What is the nature of the roots of 3x² − x + 6 = 0?
questions.e: The discriminant is b² − 4ac = (−1)² − 4(3)(6) = −71. It is negative, so there are no real roots.

questions.s: What is the minimum value of x² − 6x + 5?
questions.e: Complete the square: x² − 6x + 5 = (x − 3)² − 4. The square is at least 0, so the minimum is −4. 5 is the constant term, not the minimum.

questions.s: What is the nature of the roots of 2x² + x + 8 = 0?
questions.e: The discriminant is b² − 4ac = 1² − 4(2)(8) = −63. It is negative, so there are no real roots.

questions.s: If x + y = 12 and 3x + 2y = 31, what is the value of x?
questions.e: From x + y = 12, y = 12 − x. Substituting: 3x + 2(12 − x) = 31, so x = 7 and x = 7. 5 is the value of y.

questions.s: If f(x) = x² − 2x − 4, what is the value of f(5)?
questions.e: Substitute x = 5: (5)² − 2(5) − 4 = 25 − 10 − 4 = 11. 31 has a sign slip on the x term.

questions.s: Which inequality is equivalent to 1 − 5x > 0?
questions.e: Subtract 1: −5x > −1. Dividing by −5 reverses the sign, so x < 1/5. x > 1/5 forgets to reverse the inequality when dividing by a negative number.

questions.s: Solve for x: √(x + 13) = 6
questions.e: Square both sides: x + 13 = 36, so x = 23. −7 forgets to square both sides.

questions.s: Evaluate without a calculator: 41² − 39²
questions.e: Use a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b): (41 + 39)(41 − 39) = 80 × 2 = 160. 4 squares the difference instead of using (a + b)(a − b).

questions.s: Solve for x: x/2 + x/3 = 10
questions.e: Multiply by the common denominator 6: 3x + 2x = 60, so 5x = 60 and x = 12. 60 stops after multiplying both sides by 6, without combining and dividing by the x-coefficient.

questions.s: The sum of three consecutive integers is 123. What is the largest of them?
questions.e: Let the smallest be x. Then the numbers are x, x + 1, x + 2, so 3x + 3 = 123 and x = 40. The largest is 42. 40 is the smallest of the numbers.

questions.s: Simplify: p¹² × p⁴ ÷ (p³)⁴
questions.e: (p³)⁴ = p¹². So the expression is p¹² × p⁴ ÷ p¹² = p⁴. p⁹ treats the bracketed power as a sum of indices.

questions.s: Solve for x: 9x + 12 = 5x + 56
questions.e: Collect x-terms on one side: 4x = 56 − 12 = 44, so x = 11. −11 has the wrong sign because the constants were moved the wrong way.

questions.s: The length of a rectangular garden plot is 6 m more than its width. Its perimeter is 48 m. What is its area in m²?
questions.e: Let the width be x: 2(x + x + 6) = 48, so 4x + 12 = 48 and x = 9. Length = 15, area = 15 × 9 = 135 m². 81 uses the width as if it were a square.

questions.s: The sum of two numbers is 125 and their difference is 27. What is the larger number?
questions.e: Adding the two equations gives 2x = 125 + 27 = 152, so the larger number is 76. 49 is the smaller number.

questions.s: If a + b = 6 and ab = 8, find (a − b)².
questions.e: (a − b)² = (a + b)² − 4ab = 36 − 32 = 4. 68 adds 4ab instead of subtracting it.
The product is a difference of squares: (√13)² − (√3)² = 13 − 3 = 10. 16 adds the numbers instead of subtracting.

questions.s: Simplify: 3/(√5 − √2)
questions.e: Multiply top and bottom by √5 + √2. The denominator becomes 5 − 2 = 3, so the value is 3(√5 + √2)/3 = √5 + √2. √5 − √2 uses the original sign instead of its conjugate.

questions.s: A father is 6 times as old as his son. The sum of their ages is 91 years. How old is the father?
questions.e: Let the son be x; the father is 6x. Then 6x + x = 91, so x = 13 and the father is 6 × 13 = 78 years. 13 is the son's age.

questions.s: Iqra spends 1/4 of her pocket money on books and 1/5 on snacks. She has Rs 1,100 left. How much did she have at first, in rupees?
questions.e: The fraction left is 1 − 1/4 − 1/5 = 11/20. So she had 1,100 ÷ 11/20 = Rs 2,000. 9,900 multiplies by the sum of the denominators.

questions.s: If f(x) = 3x² − 4x − 8, what is the value of f(5)?
questions.e: Substitute x = 5: 3(5)² − 4(5) − 8 = 75 − 20 − 8 = 47. 87 has a sign slip on the x term.

questions.s: A father is 4 times as old as his son. The sum of their ages is 70 years. How old is the father?
questions.e: Let the son be x; the father is 4x. Then 4x + x = 70, so x = 14 and the father is 4 × 14 = 56 years. 14 is the son's age.

questions.s: What is the sum of the roots of 3x² − 13x + 5 = 0?
questions.e: For ax² + bx + c = 0 the sum of roots is −b/a = −(−13)/3 = 13/3. −13/3 has the wrong sign.

questions.s: What is the discriminant of 4x² − 6x + 4 = 0?
questions.e: Discriminant = b² − 4ac = (−6)² − 4(4)(4) = 36 − 64 = −28. 100 adds 4ac instead of subtracting it.

questions.s: The length of a rectangular garden plot is 9 m more than its width. Its perimeter is 34 m. What is its area in m²?
questions.e: Let the width be x: 2(x + x + 9) = 34, so 4x + 18 = 34 and x = 4. Length = 13, area = 13 × 4 = 52 m². 16 uses the width as if it were a square.

questions.s: What is the discriminant of 5x² + 6x − 7 = 0?
questions.e: Discriminant = b² − 4ac = 6² − 4(5)(−7) = 36 + 140 = 176. −104 adds 4ac instead of subtracting it.

questions.s: What is the smallest integer x satisfying 6x − 9 > 35?
questions.e: Add 9: 6x > 44, so x > 22/3. The smallest integer greater than 22/3 is 8. 7 is the integer below the boundary, which fails the inequality.

questions.s: Simplify: m²⁰ × m⁷ ÷ (m⁵)⁴
questions.e: (m⁵)⁴ = m²⁰. So the expression is m²⁰ × m⁷ ÷ m²⁰ = m⁷. m¹⁸ treats the bracketed power as a sum of indices.

questions.s: For what value of k does 3x² − 36x + k = 0 have equal roots?
questions.e: Equal roots need the discriminant b² − 4ac = 0: (−36)² − 4(3)k = 0, so k = 1,296/12 = 108. 216 uses b² ÷ 2a instead of b² ÷ 4a.

questions.s: Without solving, if α and β are the roots of x² − 4x + 14 = 0, what is the value of 1/α + 1/β?
questions.e: 1/α + 1/β = (α + β)/(αβ) = 4/14 = 2/7, using sum = 4 and product = 14. 7/2 is the reciprocal of the correct fraction.

questions.s: What is the minimum value of x² − 8x + 26?
questions.e: Complete the square: x² − 8x + 26 = (x − 4)² + 10. The square is at least 0, so the minimum is 10. 26 is the constant term, not the minimum.

questions.s: If 5x + 16 = 56, what is the value of x?
questions.e: Move the constant across: 5x = 56 − 16 = 40. Dividing by 5 gives x = 8. 40 is 5x, the value before dividing by 5.

questions.s: If x + y = 19 and x − y = 7, what is the value of 4x + 3y?
questions.e: Solving gives x = 13 and y = 6. Then 4x + 3y = 52 + 18 = 70. 97 substitutes the sum and difference directly for x and y.

questions.s: What is the sum of the roots of 2x² − 6x + 4 = 0?
questions.e: For ax² + bx + c = 0 the sum of roots is −b/a = −(−6)/2 = 3. −3 has the wrong sign.

questions.s: What is the smallest integer x satisfying 4x − 4 > 39?
questions.e: Add 4: 4x > 43, so x > 43/4. The smallest integer greater than 43/4 is 11. 10 is the integer below the boundary, which fails the inequality.

questions.s: If x + 1/x = 3, what is the value of x² + 1/x²?
questions.e: Square both sides: x² + 2 + 1/x² = 9, so x² + 1/x² = 9 − 2 = 7. 9 forgets to subtract 2.

questions.s: Simplify: √108 − √27
questions.e: Take out square factors: √108 = 6√3 and √27 = 3√3. So the expression is (6 − 3)√3 = 3√3. √81 adds or subtracts the numbers under the roots.

questions.s: Find the value of log₅ 25.
questions.e: 25 = 5², so the logarithm to base 5 is the index 2. 5 is the number divided by the base, not the index.

questions.s: Six times a number, less 15, is equal to four times the number, plus 5. What is the number?
questions.e: Form 6x − 15 = 4x + 5. Then 2x = 20, so x = 10. −5 subtracts the constants instead of adding them.

questions.s: y varies directly as x, and y = 9 when x = 3. What is y when x = 12?
questions.e: y = kx with k = 9/3 = 3. When x = 12, y = 3 × 12 = 36. 27 multiplies the given values, treating the variation as inverse.

questions.s: A taxi in Rawalpindi charges Rs 100 as a fixed fare plus Rs 25 for each kilometre. If the total fare is Rs 500, how many kilometres were travelled?
questions.e: Remove the fixed fare: 500 − 100 = 400. Dividing by Rs 25 per km gives 16 km. 20 divides the full fare without removing the fixed charge.

questions.s: Solve for x: 7x − 3 = x + 21
questions.e: Collect x-terms on one side: 6x = 21 + 3 = 24, so x = 4. 3 comes from adding the x-terms instead of subtracting them.

questions.s: If x = 4 and y = 2, what is the value of 4x² + 4xy?
questions.e: x² = 16, so 4x² = 64. xy = 8, so 4xy gives +4(8) = 32. The total is 96. 32 reverses the sign of the xy term.

questions.s: If 2x − 1 = 35, what is the value of x?
questions.e: Move the constant across: 2x = 35 + 1 = 36. Dividing by 2 gives x = 18. 36 is 2x, the value before dividing by 2.

questions.s: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 90. What is the larger integer?
questions.e: Let the integers be x and x + 1: x² + x − 90 = 0, which factorises as (x − 9)(x + 10) = 0. The positive solution is x = 9, so the larger integer is 10. 9 is the smaller integer.

questions.s: What is the remainder when x³ + 2x² + 3x + 6 is divided by (x + 1)?
questions.e: By the remainder theorem, substitute x = −1: (−1)³ + 2(−1)² + 3(−1) + 6 = −1 + 2 − 3 + 6 = 4. 12 substitutes x = 1, the wrong sign for the zero of the divisor.

questions.s: If x + 1/x = 8, what is the value of x² + 1/x²?
questions.e: Square both sides: x² + 2 + 1/x² = 64, so x² + 1/x² = 64 − 2 = 62. 64 forgets to subtract 2.

questions.s: The equation |x − 6| = 1 has two solutions. What is their product?
questions.e: x = 6 ± 1, so the solutions are 7 and 5. The product is 35. 37 adds the squares.

questions.s: If 2 to the power x equals 32, what is x?
questions.e: 32 = 2⁵, so x = 5. 16 is the number divided by the base.

questions.s: If (x − 1) is a factor of x³ + kx² − 2x − 4, what is the value of k?
questions.e: A factor means the polynomial is zero at x = 1: (1)³ + k(1)² − 2(1) − 4 = 0, so k = 5. −5 has the wrong sign.

questions.s: What is the larger root of x² + 12x + 32 = 0?
questions.e: Find two numbers with sum −12 and product 32: −4 and −8, so the equation factorises as (x + 4)(x + 8) = 0. The larger root is −4. 4 is the root with its sign reversed, a slip when reading factors such as (x − a).

questions.s: Evaluate without a calculator: 104² − 96²
questions.e: Use a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b): (104 + 96)(104 − 96) = 200 × 8 = 1,600. 64 squares the difference instead of using (a + b)(a − b).

questions.s: 2 rulers and 2 markers cost Rs 210. 2 rulers and 4 markers cost Rs 268. What is the price of one marker, in rupees?
questions.e: Let one ruler cost x and one marker cost y: 2x + 2y = 210 and 2x + 4y = 268. Eliminating one unknown gives x = 76 and y = 29. 76 is the price of one ruler.

questions.s: What is the larger root of x² + 11x + 28 = 0?
questions.e: Find two numbers with sum −11 and product 28: −4 and −7, so the equation factorises as (x + 4)(x + 7) = 0. The larger root is −4. 4 is the root with its sign reversed, a slip when reading factors such as (x − a).

questions.s: How many integers x satisfy |3x| < 11?
questions.e: |3x| < 11 means −11 < 3x < 11, so −11/3 < x < 11/3. The integers strictly inside this range number 7. 8 is one more than the integers actually inside the range.
The product is a difference of squares: (√10)² − (√7)² = 10 − 7 = 3. 17 adds the numbers instead of subtracting.

questions.s: If 5 to the power x equals 125, what is x?
questions.e: 125 = 5³, so x = 3. 25 is the number divided by the base.

questions.s: Evaluate: 1,000 raised to the power (−2/3)
questions.e: A fractional index m/n means the nth root raised to the power m. The cube root of 1,000 is 10, and 10² = 100; the negative index then takes the reciprocal, giving 1/100. 10 is only the cube root, without applying the power 2.

questions.s: Without solving, what is the product of the roots of 4x² + 6x + 9 = 0?
questions.e: For ax² + bx + c = 0 the product of roots is c/a = 9/4. −9/4 has the wrong sign.

questions.s: If x − 1/x = 6, what is the value of x² + 1/x²?
questions.e: Square both sides: x² − 2 + 1/x² = 36, so x² + 1/x² = 36 + 2 = 38. 34 uses the rule for x + 1/x.

questions.s: What is the discriminant of 3x² − 7x − 4 = 0?
questions.e: Discriminant = b² − 4ac = (−7)² − 4(3)(−4) = 49 + 48 = 97. 1 adds 4ac instead of subtracting it.

questions.s: What is the smallest integer x satisfying 6x + 4 > 35?
questions.e: Subtract 4: 6x > 31, so x > 31/6. The smallest integer greater than 31/6 is 6. 5 is the integer below the boundary, which fails the inequality.

questions.s: The product of two consecutive positive even integers is 624. What is the smaller one?
questions.e: Let the integers be x and x + 2: x² + 2x − 624 = 0, which factorises as (x − 24)(x + 26) = 0. The positive root is 24, the smaller integer. 26 is the larger even integer.

questions.s: The equation |x − 3| = 2 has two solutions. What is their product?
questions.e: x = 3 ± 2, so the solutions are 5 and 1. The product is 5. 13 adds the squares.

questions.s: Solve for x: 8x + 9 = 6x + 29
questions.e: Collect x-terms on one side: 2x = 29 − 9 = 20, so x = 10. −10 has the wrong sign because the constants were moved the wrong way.

questions.s: What is the smaller root of x² − 13x + 22 = 0?
questions.e: Find two numbers with sum 13 and product 22: 11 and 2, so the equation factorises as (x − 11)(x − 2) = 0. The smaller root is 2. −2 is the root with its sign reversed, a slip when reading factors such as (x − a).

questions.s: Bilal is 3 years older than Maryam. In 9 years the sum of their ages will be 85 years. How old is Bilal now?
questions.e: Their present ages sum to 85 − 2 × 9 = 67. With a difference of 3, Bilal's age is (67 + 3)/2 = 35. 32 is Maryam's present age.

questions.s: If 5x − 1 = −26, what is the value of x?
questions.e: Move the constant across: 5x = −26 + 1 = −25. Dividing by 5 gives x = −5. −25 is 5x, the value before dividing by 5.

questions.s: What is the value of log₂ 16 + log₂ 4?
questions.e: log₂ 16 = 4 and log₂ 4 = 2, so the sum is 6. Equivalently log₂ (16 × 4) = log₂ 64 = 6. 8 multiplies the two logarithms.

questions.s: A bag of wheat weighs 69 kg more than a bag of rice. Together the two bags weigh 83 kg. What is the weight of the wheat bag in kg?
questions.e: If the rice bag weighs x kg, the wheat bag weighs x + 69. Then 2x + 69 = 83, so x = 7 and the wheat bag weighs 7 + 69 = 76 kg. 7 is the weight of the rice bag.

questions.s: If a − b = 2 and ab = 8, find (a + b)².
questions.e: (a + b)² = (a − b)² + 4ab = 4 + 32 = 36. 20 uses 2ab where 4ab is needed.

questions.s: A triangular field has an area of 210 m² and a base of 28 m. What is its perpendicular height?
questions.e: Area = ½ × base × height, so height = 2 × 210 ÷ 28 = 15 m. 30 m doubles the correct height.

questions.s: What is the total surface area of a cuboid measuring 13 cm by 5 cm by 5 cm?
questions.e: Surface area = 2(lw + wh + hl) = 2(65 + 25 + 65) = 310 cm². 155 cm² forgets to double the face areas.

questions.s: A window is made of a rectangle 14 cm wide and 24 cm tall with a semicircle on top whose diameter is the rectangle's top edge. Taking π = 22/7, what is the total area of the window?
questions.e: Rectangle = 14 × 24 = 336 cm². The semicircle has radius 7 cm, so its area is ½ × 22/7 × 7² = 77 cm². Total = 413 cm². 490 cm² uses a full circle instead of a semicircle.

questions.s: A chord is 20 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 25 cm. What is the length of the chord?
questions.e: Half the chord is √(25² − 20²) = 15 cm, so the chord is 2 × 15 = 30 cm. 15 cm is only half the chord.

questions.s: What is the area of a sector of angle 40° in a circle of radius 3 cm, in terms of π?
questions.e: Sector area = (θ/360) × πr² = (40/360) × π × 9 = π cm². 2π/3 cm² uses the arc-length formula.

questions.s: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides in the ratio 1 : 3. The smaller triangle has an area of 9 cm². What is the area of the larger triangle?
questions.e: Areas of similar figures are in the ratio of the squares of the sides: 1 : 9. So the larger area is 9 × 9/1 = 81 cm². 27 cm² scales the area by the ratio of the sides instead of its square.

questions.s: What is the length of the longest straight line that can be drawn inside a cuboid measuring 4 cm by 6 cm by 12 cm?
questions.e: The space diagonal is √(l² + w² + h²) = √(16 + 36 + 144) = √196 = 14 cm. 22 cm adds the three edges.

questions.s: Two angles of a triangle measure 34° and 68°. What is the third angle?
questions.e: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. So the third angle is 180° − 34° − 68° = 78°. 258° uses 360° instead of 180° as the angle sum.

questions.s: Taking π = 22/7, what is the curved surface area of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 2 cm?
questions.e: Curved surface area = 2πrh = 2 × 22/7 × 7 × 2 = 88 cm². 308 cm² is the volume.

questions.s: A cube has a volume of 1,728 cm³. What is its total surface area?
questions.e: The edge is the cube root of 1,728, which is 12 cm. Surface area = 6 × 12² = 864 cm². 144 cm² is the area of one face only.

questions.s: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 1 : 4 : 5. What is the smallest angle?
questions.e: The ratio parts add up to 10, and one part is 180° ÷ 10 = 18°. The smallest angle is 1 × 18° = 18°. 90° is the largest angle.

questions.s: What is the total surface area of a closed cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 7 cm, in terms of π?
questions.e: Total surface area = 2πr(r + h) = 2π × 7 × (7 + 7) = 196π cm². 98π cm² is the curved surface only.

questions.s: One side of a triangle is extended, making an exterior angle of 131° at a vertex. One of the two interior opposite angles is 61°. What is the other interior opposite angle?
questions.e: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles, so the other angle is 131° − 61° = 70°. 49° is the interior angle at the same vertex.

questions.s: Two adjacent angles on a straight line are in the ratio 5 : 7. What is the larger angle?
questions.e: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. One part is 180° ÷ 12 = 15°, so the larger angle is 7 × 15° = 105°. 75° is the smaller angle.

questions.s: A cone has a base radius of 12 cm and a vertical height of 16 cm. What is its curved surface area, in terms of π?
questions.e: The slant height is √(12² + 16²) = 20 cm. Curved surface area = πrl = π × 12 × 20 = 240π cm². 192π cm² uses the vertical height instead of the slant height.

questions.s: What is the size of each interior angle of a regular dodecagon?
questions.e: The interior angle sum is 10 × 180° = 1,800°. Divided equally among 12 angles, each is 150°. 30° is the exterior angle.

questions.s: A 20 m ladder leans against a boundary wall. Its foot is 12 m from the base of the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach?
questions.e: The wall, ground and ladder form a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse 20 m. The height is √(20² − 12²) = √256 = 16 m. 8 m subtracts the lengths instead of the squares.

questions.s: A rectangular sheet of metal measures 20 cm by 21 cm. What is the length of its diagonal?
questions.e: By Pythagoras' theorem the hypotenuse is √(20² + 21²) = √841 = 29 cm. 41 cm adds the two sides without using Pythagoras' theorem.

questions.s: An arc of a circle subtends an angle of 170° at the centre. What angle does it subtend at a point on the remaining part of the circle?
questions.e: The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre: 170° ÷ 2 = 85°. 170° is the angle at the centre.

questions.s: A square floor measures 4 m by 4 m. How many square tiles of side 20 cm are needed to cover it exactly?
questions.e: Along the length 400 cm ÷ 20 cm = 20 tiles; along the width 400 ÷ 20 = 20 tiles. Total = 20 × 20 = 400. 80 converts only one of the lengths.

questions.s: A rectangular field measures 80 m by 30 m. What is the cost of fencing all four sides at Rs 120 per metre?
questions.e: Perimeter = 2(80 + 30) = 220 m. Cost = 220 × 120 = Rs 26,400. Rs 288,000 uses the area instead of the perimeter.

questions.s: What is the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon?
questions.e: The interior angle sum is (n − 2) × 180°. A pentagon has 5 sides, so the sum is 3 × 180° = 540°. 900° uses n instead of n − 2.

questions.s: A right-angled triangle has perpendicular sides of 9 cm and 40 cm. What is the length of its hypotenuse?
questions.e: By Pythagoras' theorem the hypotenuse is √(9² + 40²) = √1,681 = 41 cm. 49 cm adds the two sides without using Pythagoras' theorem.

questions.s: What is the length of an arc of a circle of radius 20 cm that subtends an angle of 150° at the centre, in terms of π?
questions.e: Arc length = (θ/360) × 2πr = (150/360) × 2π × 20 = 50π/3 cm. 500π/3 cm uses the sector-area formula.

questions.s: Each edge of a cube is multiplied by 3. By what factor is its volume multiplied?
questions.e: Volume depends on the cube of the edge, so it is multiplied by 3³ = 27. 3 is the factor for the edge.

questions.s: The midpoints of the three sides of a triangle of area 120 cm² are joined to form a smaller triangle. What is the area of the smaller triangle?
questions.e: Each side of the smaller triangle is half the original side, so its area is (½)² = ¼ of the original: 120 ÷ 4 = 30 cm². 60 cm² halves the area instead of quartering it.

questions.s: What is the total surface area of a cuboid measuring 6 cm by 7 cm by 5 cm?
questions.e: Surface area = 2(lw + wh + hl) = 2(42 + 35 + 30) = 214 cm². 107 cm² forgets to double the face areas.

questions.s: The hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle is 15 cm and one of the other sides is 9 cm. What is the length of the third side?
questions.e: The missing side is √(15² − 9²) = √144 = 12 cm. 6 cm subtracts the lengths instead of the squares.

questions.s: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?
questions.e: The interior angle sum is (n − 2) × 180°. A hexagon has 6 sides, so the sum is 4 × 180° = 720°. 1,080° uses n instead of n − 2.

questions.s: The diagonals of a rhombus are 16 cm and 30 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.e: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, so each side is √(8² + 15²) = 17 cm. The perimeter is 4 × 17 = 68 cm. 92 cm treats the diagonals as the sides of a rectangle.

questions.s: What is the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and perpendicular height 21 cm?
questions.e: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 21 = 105 cm². 210 cm² forgets the factor ½.

questions.s: Taking π = 22/7, what is the circumference of a circle of radius 7 cm?
questions.e: Circumference = 2πr = 2 × 22/7 × 7 = 44 cm. 154 cm is the area formula applied to the circumference.

questions.s: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 4:30?
questions.e: The hour hand is at 30° × 4 + 0.5° × 30 = 135° from 12, and the minute hand is at 6° × 30 = 180°. The difference is 45°, and the smaller angle is 45°. 60° ignores the movement of the hour hand between the hour marks.

questions.s: A point P is 10 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 6 cm. What is the length of the tangent drawn from P to the circle?
questions.e: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so tangent² = 10² − 6² = 64. The tangent is 8 cm. 4 cm subtracts the radius from the distance.

questions.s: What is the surface area of a sphere of radius 7 cm, in terms of π?
questions.e: Surface area = 4πr² = 4 × π × 7² = 196π cm². 49π cm² uses πr², the area of a great circle.

questions.s: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides of 13 cm and a base of 10 cm. What is its area?
questions.e: The height is √(13² − 5²) = 12 cm. Area = ½ × 10 × 12 = 60 cm². 120 cm² forgets the factor ½.

questions.s: What is the length of the diagonal of a square of side 8 cm?
questions.e: The diagonal splits the square into two right triangles: d = √(8² + 8²) = √128 = 8√2 cm. 16 cm doubles the side.

questions.s: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides of 10 cm and a base of 12 cm. What is its area?
questions.e: The height is √(10² − 6²) = 8 cm. Area = ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 cm². 96 cm² forgets the factor ½.

questions.s: Two angles of a triangle measure 25° and 55°. What is the third angle?
questions.e: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. So the third angle is 180° − 25° − 55° = 100°. 280° uses 360° instead of 180° as the angle sum.

questions.s: A square is drawn inside a circle of radius 11 cm so that all four corners lie on the circle. What is the area of the square?
questions.e: The diagonal of the square is the diameter 22 cm, so area = ½ × diagonal² = ½ × 484 = 242 cm². 121 cm² uses the radius as the side.

questions.s: A vertical pole 1 m tall casts a shadow 5 m long. At the same time a tree casts a shadow 45 m long. How tall is the tree?
questions.e: Heights are proportional to shadow lengths: tree/1 = 45/5, so the tree is 1 × 45/5 = 9 m. 41 m adds the difference in shadow lengths to the pole's height.

questions.s: The circumference of a circle is 6π cm. What is its area in terms of π?
questions.e: 2πr = 6π, so r = 3 cm. Area = πr² = 9π cm². 18π cm² is double the area.

questions.s: How many diagonals does a convex polygon with 6 sides have?
questions.e: Each vertex joins to 3 non-adjacent vertices, giving 6 × 3 = 18, but each diagonal is counted twice. So there are 9. 15 counts every pair of vertices, including the sides.

questions.s: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 4 : 5 : 9. What is the largest angle?
questions.e: The ratio parts add up to 18, and one part is 180° ÷ 18 = 10°. The largest angle is 9 × 10° = 90°. 40° is the smallest angle.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, D lies on AB and E lies on AC so that DE is parallel to BC. AD = 3 cm, DB = 2 cm and BC = 10 cm. What is the length of DE?
questions.e: Triangles ADE and ABC are similar, so DE/BC = AD/AB = 3/5. Hence DE = 10 × 3/5 = 6 cm. 15 cm uses DB instead of AB in the ratio.

questions.s: The hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle is 13 cm and one of the other sides is 5 cm. What is the length of the third side?
questions.e: The missing side is √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12 cm. 8 cm subtracts the lengths instead of the squares.

questions.s: The diagonals of a rhombus are 6 cm and 8 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.e: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, so each side is √(3² + 4²) = 5 cm. The perimeter is 4 × 5 = 20 cm. 28 cm treats the diagonals as the sides of a rectangle.

questions.s: The parallel sides of a trapezium are 15 cm and 23 cm long, and the distance between them is 9 cm. What is its area?
questions.e: Area = ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × height = ½ × (15 + 23) × 9 = 171 cm². 342 cm² forgets the factor ½.

questions.s: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of co-interior angles measure (2x + 14)° and (4x + 40)°. What is the larger angle?
questions.e: Co-interior angles add up to 180°: (2x + 14) + (4x + 40) = 180, so 6x + 54 = 180 and x = 21. The angles are 56° and 124°. 56° is the smaller angle.

questions.s: Taking π = 22/7, what is the curved surface area of a cylinder of radius 28 cm and height 5 cm?
questions.e: Curved surface area = 2πrh = 2 × 22/7 × 28 × 5 = 880 cm². 12,320 cm² is the volume.

questions.s: What is the length of an arc of a circle of radius 20 cm that subtends an angle of 90° at the centre, in terms of π?
questions.e: Arc length = (θ/360) × 2πr = (90/360) × 2π × 20 = 10π cm. 100π cm uses the sector-area formula.

questions.s: What is the area of a circle of radius 5 cm, in terms of π?
questions.e: Area = πr² = π × 5² = 25π cm². 10π cm² is the circumference, not the area.

questions.s: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 30°. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.e: The exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°. So the number of sides is 360 ÷ 30 = 12. 150 is the interior angle.

questions.s: What is the size of each interior angle of a regular pentagon?
questions.e: The interior angle sum is 3 × 180° = 540°. Divided equally among 5 angles, each is 108°. 72° is the exterior angle.

questions.s: A chord is 24 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 25 cm. What is the length of the chord?
questions.e: Half the chord is √(25² − 24²) = 7 cm, so the chord is 2 × 7 = 14 cm. 7 cm is only half the chord.

questions.s: A rectangular lawn is 24 m long and 12 m wide. A flower bed 3 m wide is laid all the way round just inside its edge. What is the area of the flower bed in m²?
questions.e: The inner lawn is 18 m by 6 m, area 108 m². Subtracting from the full 288 m² leaves 180 m². 216 counts the corner squares twice.

questions.s: Two tangents PA and PB are drawn from an external point P to a circle with centre O, and angle APB is 40°. What is angle AOB?
questions.e: Angles OAP and OBP are right angles (tangent ⟂ radius). In quadrilateral OAPB, angle AOB = 360° − 90° − 90° − 40° = 140°. 40° assumes the two angles are equal.

questions.s: What is the height of an equilateral triangle of side 8 cm?
questions.e: The height splits the triangle into two triangles with angles 30°, 60° and 90°: h = √(8² − 4²) = √48 = 4√3 cm. 8√3 cm omits the factor ½.

questions.s: What is the area of a sector of angle 270° in a circle of radius 12 cm, in terms of π?
questions.e: Sector area = (θ/360) × πr² = (270/360) × π × 144 = 108π cm². 18π cm² uses the arc-length formula.

questions.s: A rectangular lawn is 27 m long and 12 m wide. A flower bed 3 m wide is laid all the way round just inside its edge. What is the area of the flower bed in m²?
questions.e: The inner lawn is 21 m by 6 m, area 126 m². Subtracting from the full 324 m² leaves 198 m². 234 counts the corner squares twice.

questions.s: An angle is 34° less than three times its complement. What is the angle?
questions.e: Let the complement be x; the angle is 90 − x. Then 90 − x = 3x − 34, so 4x = 124 and x = 31. The angle is 59°. 31° is its complement.

questions.s: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides in the ratio 1 : 2. The smaller triangle has an area of 7 cm². What is the area of the larger triangle?
questions.e: Areas of similar figures are in the ratio of the squares of the sides: 1 : 4. So the larger area is 7 × 4/1 = 28 cm². 14 cm² scales the area by the ratio of the sides instead of its square.

questions.s: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 156°. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.e: The exterior angle is 180° − 156° = 24°. The exterior angles total 360°, so there are 360 ÷ 24 = 15 sides. 24 is the exterior angle, not the number of sides.

questions.s: The perimeter of a square is 36 cm. What is its area?
questions.e: Each side is 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm, so the area is 9² = 81 cm². 1,296 cm² squares the perimeter.

questions.s: A courtyard is 9 m long and 8 m wide. What is the cost of paving it at Rs 80 per square metre?
questions.e: Area = 8 × 9 = 72 m². Cost = 72 × 80 = Rs 5,760. Rs 2,720 uses the perimeter instead of the area.

questions.s: In an isosceles triangle the angle between the two equal sides is 34°. What is each of the other two angles?
questions.e: The other two angles are equal and add up to 180° − 34° = 146°, so each is 73°. 146° is the sum of the two base angles.

questions.s: Taking π = 22/7, what is the circumference of a circle of radius 14 cm?
questions.e: Circumference = 2πr = 2 × 22/7 × 14 = 88 cm. 616 cm is the area formula applied to the circumference.

questions.s: A rectangular tank measures 5 m by 4 m by 2 m. Water flows into it at 800 litres per minute. How many minutes does it take to fill the empty tank? (1 m³ = 1,000 litres)
questions.e: Volume = 5 × 4 × 2 = 40 m³ = 40,000 litres. Time = 40,000 ÷ 800 = 50 minutes. 500 takes 10,000 litres to a cubic metre.

questions.s: What is the distance between the points (4, −1) and (−8, −17) on a coordinate plane, in units?
questions.e: The horizontal difference is 12 and the vertical difference is 16. Distance = √(12² + 16²) = √400 = 20 units. 28 adds the horizontal and vertical differences.

questions.s: What is the length of the longest straight line that can be drawn inside a cuboid measuring 8 cm by 8 cm by 14 cm?
questions.e: The space diagonal is √(l² + w² + h²) = √(64 + 64 + 196) = √324 = 18 cm. 30 cm adds the three edges.
