questions.s: Taking π = 22/7, the area of a circle is 154 cm². What is its radius?
questions.e: πr² = 154 gives r² = 154 × 7/22 = 49, so r = 7 cm. 14 cm is the diameter.

questions.s: A 17 m ladder reaches a point 15 m above the ground on a house. How far is the foot of the ladder from the wall?
questions.e: The distance is √(17² − 15²) = √64 = 8 m. 2 m subtracts the lengths instead of the squares.

questions.s: A point P is 5 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 3 cm. What is the length of the tangent drawn from P to the circle?
questions.e: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so tangent² = 5² − 3² = 16. The tangent is 4 cm. 2 cm subtracts the radius from the distance.

questions.s: The length of a rectangle is 3 times its width and its perimeter is 40 cm. What is its area?
questions.e: Let the width be x: 2(3x + x) = 40, so x = 5 and the length is 15. Area = 15 × 5 = 75 cm². 225 cm² squares the length.

questions.s: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of alternate interior angles measure (2x + 9)° and (3x − 13)°. What is the size of each angle?
questions.e: Alternate interior angles are equal: 2x + 9 = 3x − 13, so x = 22. Each angle is 53°. 127° is the supplement, the value for co-interior angles.

questions.s: What is the length of the diagonal of a square of side 13 cm?
questions.e: The diagonal splits the square into two right triangles: d = √(13² + 13²) = √338 = 13√2 cm. 26 cm doubles the side.

questions.s: A solid sphere of radius 2 cm is melted and recast into small spheres of radius 1 cm. How many small spheres are made?
questions.e: Volume of a sphere is proportional to r³, so the number is (2/1)³ = 8. 4 compares surface areas.

questions.s: A solid sphere of radius 9 cm is melted and recast into small spheres of radius 3 cm. How many small spheres are made?
questions.e: Volume of a sphere is proportional to r³, so the number is (9/3)³ = 27. 9 compares surface areas.

questions.s: What is the area of a triangle whose sides are 8 cm, 15 cm and 17 cm?
questions.e: Use Heron's formula: s = 20, so area = √(20 × 12 × 5 × 3) = √3,600 = 60 cm². 20 cm² is the semi-perimeter, not the area.

questions.s: Taking π = 22/7, how many complete turns does a wheel of radius 42 cm make while covering 660 m?
questions.e: One turn covers 2πr = 2 × 22/7 × 42 = 264 cm. The distance is 660 m = 66,000 cm, so the number of turns is 66,000 ÷ 264 = 250. 500 uses πr instead of 2πr as the distance per turn.

questions.s: A chord of length 48 cm is drawn in a circle of radius 25 cm. What is the perpendicular distance of the chord from the centre?
questions.e: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, forming a right triangle with hypotenuse 25 and one side 24. The distance is √(25² − 24²) = 7 cm. 1 cm subtracts the half-chord from the radius.

questions.s: The length of a rectangle is 2 times its width and its perimeter is 36 cm. What is its area?
questions.e: Let the width be x: 2(2x + x) = 36, so x = 6 and the length is 12. Area = 12 × 6 = 72 cm². 144 cm² squares the length.

questions.s: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of co-interior angles measure (x + 3)° and (4x + 32)°. What is the larger angle?
questions.e: Co-interior angles add up to 180°: (x + 3) + (4x + 32) = 180, so 5x + 35 = 180 and x = 29. The angles are 32° and 148°. 32° is the smaller angle.

questions.s: A right-angled triangle has perpendicular sides of 24 cm and 45 cm. What is the length of its hypotenuse?
questions.e: By Pythagoras' theorem the hypotenuse is √(24² + 45²) = √2,601 = 51 cm. 69 cm adds the two sides without using Pythagoras' theorem.

questions.s: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides in the ratio 1 : 3. The smaller triangle has an area of 7 cm². What is the area of the larger triangle?
questions.e: Areas of similar figures are in the ratio of the squares of the sides: 1 : 9. So the larger area is 7 × 9/1 = 63 cm². 21 cm² scales the area by the ratio of the sides instead of its square.

questions.s: A solid metal cube of edge 4 cm is melted and recast into small cubes of edge 2 cm. How many small cubes are made?
questions.e: Volumes are compared: 4³ ÷ 2³ = (4/2)³ = 2³ = 8. 4 compares the areas of the faces.

questions.s: Taking π = 22/7, what is the circumference of a circle of radius 42 cm?
questions.e: Circumference = 2πr = 2 × 22/7 × 42 = 264 cm. 5,544 cm is the area formula applied to the circumference.

questions.s: What is the size of each interior angle of a regular octagon?
questions.e: The interior angle sum is 6 × 180° = 1,080°. Divided equally among 8 angles, each is 135°. 45° is the exterior angle.

questions.s: The diagonals of a rhombus are 24 cm and 32 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.e: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, so each side is √(12² + 16²) = 20 cm. The perimeter is 4 × 20 = 80 cm. 112 cm treats the diagonals as the sides of a rectangle.

questions.s: A and B lie on a circle with centre O, and angle AOB is 80°. What is angle OAB?
questions.e: OA = OB (radii), so triangle OAB is isosceles. Angle OAB = (180° − 80°)/2 = 50°. 100° is the sum of the two base angles.

questions.s: An angle is 38° less than three times its complement. What is the angle?
questions.e: Let the complement be x; the angle is 90 − x. Then 90 − x = 3x − 38, so 4x = 128 and x = 32. The angle is 58°. 32° is its complement.

questions.s: A cone has a base radius of 3 cm and a vertical height of 4 cm. What is its curved surface area, in terms of π?
questions.e: The slant height is √(3² + 4²) = 5 cm. Curved surface area = πrl = π × 3 × 5 = 15π cm². 12π cm² uses the vertical height instead of the slant height.

questions.s: What is the length of an arc of a circle of radius 6 cm that subtends an angle of 30° at the centre, in terms of π?
questions.e: Arc length = (θ/360) × 2πr = (30/360) × 2π × 6 = π cm. 3π cm uses the sector-area formula.

questions.s: What is the total surface area of a cuboid measuring 11 cm by 7 cm by 2 cm?
questions.e: Surface area = 2(lw + wh + hl) = 2(77 + 14 + 22) = 226 cm². 113 cm² forgets to double the face areas.

questions.s: Two angles of a triangle measure 29° and 84°. What is the third angle?
questions.e: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. So the third angle is 180° − 29° − 84° = 67°. 247° uses 360° instead of 180° as the angle sum.

questions.s: The table shows the number of cars sold by a showroom in six months. How many more were sold in the first three months than in the last three months?
questions.e: First three months: 429 + 446 + 347 = 1,222. Last three months: 275 + 426 + 332 = 1,033. Difference = 189. 2,255 is the total for all six months.

questions.s: The ages, in years, of 6 cricketers in a club team are 29, 22, 18, 32, 44, 53. What is the mean?
questions.e: Mean = sum ÷ number of values = 198 ÷ 6 = 33. 32 divides by one fewer than the number of values.

questions.s: The table shows the number of siblings of each of 15 students. What is the median number of siblings?
questions.e: The median is the value of student number (15 + 1)/2 = 8. Cumulative frequencies are 1, 4, 5, 14, 15, so the 8th student has 3 siblings. 2 is the middle row of the table, not the middle student.

questions.s: The mean of 6 numbers is 37. 5 of them are 41, 49, 33, 36, 30. What is the remaining number?
questions.e: The total of all 6 numbers is 6 × 37 = 222. The known numbers add up to 189, so the remaining number is 222 − 189 = 33. 37 is the mean itself.

questions.s: The table shows the number of pupils who sat and passed an annual exam in five classes. Which class had the highest pass percentage?
questions.e: Pass percentages: Class 6 50%, Class 7 80%, Class 8 45%, Class 9 90%, Class 10 85%. The highest is Class 9 (90%). Class 10 has the most passes but not the best rate.

questions.s: The mean of 5 numbers is 31. 4 of them are 27, 24, 21, 21. What is the remaining number?
questions.e: The total of all 5 numbers is 5 × 31 = 155. The known numbers add up to 93, so the remaining number is 155 − 93 = 62. 31 is the mean itself.

questions.s: The mean of 6 numbers is 15. Each number is multiplied by 3 and then 10 is added. What is the mean of the new numbers?
questions.e: Both operations apply to the mean in the same way: 3 × 15 + 10 = 55. 75 adds before multiplying.

questions.s: The table shows four students' marks in three tests. Which student improved the most from Test 1 to Test 3?
questions.e: Improvement (Test 3 − Test 1): Sana −34, Hira −4, Ayesha 11, Iqra 27. The largest is Iqra's, 27 marks.

questions.s: The table shows a family's monthly income and expenditure. In which month was the saving (income minus expenditure) the largest?
questions.e: Find the difference for each month: Jan −3, Feb 35, Mar 36, Apr 33, May −4, Jun −30. The largest, 36, is in Mar.

questions.s: The table shows the runs scored by six players of a club in one innings. What is the range of the scores?
questions.e: Range = highest − lowest = 93 − 18 = 75. 93 is the highest value.

questions.s: What is the median of the values 27, 11, 39, 45, 33, 84, 8?
questions.e: Arrange in order: 8, 11, 27, 33, 39, 45, 84. With 7 values the median is the middle one, 33. 45 is the middle value in the order given, before sorting.

questions.s: The table shows the rainfall recorded in a hill station on six days. What is the mean daily rainfall, in mm?
questions.e: Mean = 144 ÷ 6 = 24. 23 is the median, not the mean.

questions.s: The table shows a bank's deposits in four cities. In 2023, by how much (in Rs million) did the deposits of Sialkot differ from those of Rawalpindi?
questions.e: Sialkot: 142; Rawalpindi: 410. Difference = 268 million. 552 adds the two figures.

questions.s: The table shows a firm's exports and imports over six months. In which month did exports exceed imports by the largest amount?
questions.e: Find the difference for each month: Jan 52, Feb 47, Mar −19, Apr −36, May −27, Jun −7. The largest, 52, is in Jan.

questions.s: The table shows the number of goals scored by a school football team in 20 matches. What is the mean number of goals per match?
questions.e: Multiply each value by its frequency and add: 0×7 + 1×3 + 2×1 + 3×6 + 4×3 = 35. Divide by the total frequency 20: mean = 1.75. 2 averages the five values without weighting by frequency.

questions.s: The table shows the yearly sales of a mobile-phone shop. Between which two consecutive years was the increase in sales the largest?
The table shows the units of four stationery items sold in a month and the price per unit. What was the total revenue from files and markers together, in rupees?

questions.s: The table shows the number of candidates who appeared in and passed five subjects. Which subject had the highest pass percentage?
questions.e: Pass percentages: Urdu 80%, English 40%, Maths 85%, Physics 65%, Biology 75%. The highest is Maths (85%).

questions.s: The table shows the number of boys and girls on four buses during a school trip. What is the ratio of the total number of boys to the total number of girls on these buses?
questions.e: Total of the first column = 25 + 21 + 37 + 31 = 114; total of the second = 19 + 27 + 35 + 19 = 100. The ratio 114 : 100 simplifies to 57 : 50. 50 : 57 reverses the ratio.

questions.s: The table shows the number of patients treated at a clinic. What was the percentage increase from 2022 to 2023?
questions.e: Increase = 1,200 − 800 = 400. Percentage increase = 400/800 × 100 = 50%. 33.3% is the increase as a percentage of the later year.

questions.s: The table shows the orders received by a shop in six months. By how much does the highest monthly figure exceed the mean monthly figure, to the nearest whole number?
questions.e: Mean = 1,852 ÷ 6 ≈ 308.7. The highest month is 414, so it exceeds the mean by about 105. 265 uses the lowest month instead of the mean.

questions.s: The table shows the number of books read last month by each of 20 pupils. What is the mean number of books read per pupil?
questions.e: Multiply each value by its frequency and add: 1×1 + 2×11 + 3×6 + 4×1 + 5×1 = 50. Divide by the total frequency 20: mean = 2.5. 3 averages the five values without weighting by frequency.

questions.s: The mean of 6 numbers is 43. One number, 47, is replaced by another number and the mean becomes 47. What is the new number?
questions.e: The total rises by 6 × 4 = 24, so the replacement is 24 more than the old number: 47 + 24 = 71. 51 adds only the rise in the mean.

questions.s: Ayesha reads this many pages on 7 consecutive days: 56, 44, 8, 57, 23, 50, 14. What is the mean?
questions.e: Mean = sum ÷ number of values = 252 ÷ 7 = 36. 44 is the median.

questions.s: The table shows the number of children in each of 40 families. What percentage of the families have at least 2 children?
questions.e: Families with at least 2 children: 6 + 5 + 17 = 28. Percentage = 28/40 × 100 = 70%. 28% reports the count as a percentage.

questions.s: The table shows the units of four stationery items sold in a month and the price per unit. What was the total revenue from pens and folders together, in rupees?
questions.e: Revenue = units × price. Pens: 50 × 12 = 600; Folders: 180 × 30 = 5,400. Total = Rs 6,000. Rs 230 adds the units sold.

questions.s: The table shows the number of children in each of 25 families. What percentage of the families have at least 3 children?
questions.e: Families with at least 3 children: 10 + 1 = 11. Percentage = 11/25 × 100 = 44%. 11% reports the count as a percentage.

questions.s: The table shows a bank's deposits in four cities. What were the total deposits of Karachi over the three years, in Rs million?
questions.e: Add the three years for Karachi: 278 + 174 + 275 = 727. 903 is the total for Multan.

questions.s: The table shows the number of visitors to a museum in six months. How many more were there in the last three months than in the first three months?
questions.e: First three months: 449 + 252 + 266 = 967. Last three months: 468 + 387 + 233 = 1,088. Difference = 121. 2,055 is the total for all six months.

questions.s: The median of the seven numbers 48, 5, 54, 42, 51, 22, 44 is found. If 6 is added to every number, what is the new median?
questions.e: The median is 44. Adding 6 to every number shifts the median by 6: 44 + 6 = 50. 44 ignores the added amount.

questions.s: The table shows the number of siblings of each of 19 students. What is the median number of siblings?
questions.e: The median is the value of student number (19 + 1)/2 = 10. Cumulative frequencies are 4, 5, 14, 18, 19, so the 10th student has 2 siblings.

questions.s: The table shows the number of siblings of each of 25 students. What is the median number of siblings?
questions.e: The median is the value of student number (25 + 1)/2 = 13. Cumulative frequencies are 14, 15, 20, 22, 25, so the 13th student has 0 siblings. 2 is the middle row of the table, not the middle student.

questions.s: The table shows the number of students enrolled in a college. What was the percentage increase from 2017 to 2018?
questions.e: Increase = 1,200 − 800 = 400. Percentage increase = 400/800 × 100 = 50%. 33.3% is the increase as a percentage of the later year.

questions.s: The table shows a mill's production and sales over six months. In which month did production exceed sales by the largest amount?
questions.e: Find the difference for each month: Jan 2, Feb −23, Mar 16, Apr 52, May 70, Jun 11. The largest, 70, is in May.

questions.s: The mean of 9 numbers is 58. One number, 54, is replaced by another number and the mean becomes 61. What is the new number?

questions.s: The table shows the units of four stationery items sold in a month and the price per unit. What was the total revenue from pens and files together, in rupees?

questions.s: The table shows the electricity used by a household in six months. What is the mean monthly use, in units?
questions.e: Mean = 1,764 ÷ 6 = 294. 288 is the median, not the mean.

questions.s: The table shows the yearly rice production of a district. Between which two consecutive years was the increase in production the largest?
questions.e: Year-to-year changes: 2017 to 2018: +13, 2018 to 2019: 0, 2019 to 2020: +8, 2020 to 2021: +11, 2021 to 2022: −50. The largest rise is 13, from 2017 to 2018. 2020 to 2021 ends at the extreme value but is not the largest change.

questions.s: The marks scored by 7 students in a class test are 28, 18, 24, 49, 52, 47, 48. What is the mean?
questions.e: Mean = sum ÷ number of values = 266 ÷ 7 = 38. 47 is the median.

questions.s: The table shows the number of students in three sections and the mean marks of each section. What is the mean mark of all the students taken together?
questions.e: Weight each mean by its group size: (10×53 + 30×50 + 60×61) ÷ 100 = 5,690 ÷ 100 = 56.9. A simple average of the means ignores the different group sizes. 54.67 averages the three means without weighting.

questions.s: The table shows the sales of a company's four branches in one month. What percentage of the total sales came from the Sialkot branch?
questions.e: Total sales = 360 + 280 + 120 + 40 = 800 thousand. Share = 280/800 × 100 = 35%. 280% uses the sales figure as the percentage.

questions.s: The table shows the number of households in three villages and the mean monthly income in each. What is the mean monthly income of all the households taken together, in Rs thousand?
questions.e: Weight each mean by its group size: (40×33 + 20×36 + 40×71) ÷ 100 = 4,880 ÷ 100 = 48.8. A simple average of the means ignores the different group sizes. 46.67 averages the three means without weighting.

questions.s: The table shows the number of books issued by a public library. What was the percentage increase from 2018 to 2019?
questions.e: Increase = 700 − 500 = 200. Percentage increase = 200/500 × 100 = 40%. 28.6% is the increase as a percentage of the later year.

questions.s: The table shows the number of boys and girls in four classes of a school. What is the ratio of the total number of boys to the total number of girls in these classes?
questions.e: Total of the first column = 32 + 37 + 25 + 24 = 118; total of the second = 28 + 25 + 27 + 22 = 102. The ratio 118 : 102 simplifies to 59 : 51. 51 : 59 reverses the ratio.

questions.s: The mean of 8 numbers is 24. Each number is increased by 4 and then doubled. What is the mean of the new numbers?
questions.e: The mean is increased by 4 to 28, then multiplied by 2: 56. 52 multiplies before adding.

questions.s: The table shows the number of candidates who appeared in and passed a test at five centres. Which centre had the highest pass percentage?
questions.e: Pass percentages: Lahore 95%, Karachi 60%, Quetta 55%, Peshawar 65%, Multan 50%. The highest is Lahore (95%).

questions.s: The table shows the units of four stationery items sold in a month and the price per unit. What was the total revenue from folders and rulers together, in rupees?
questions.e: Revenue = units × price. Folders: 400 × 35 = 14,000; Rulers: 190 × 15 = 2,850. Total = Rs 16,850. Rs 590 adds the units sold.

questions.s: The table shows the number of patients treated at a clinic. What was the percentage increase from 2018 to 2019?
questions.e: Increase = 300 − 240 = 60. Percentage increase = 60/240 × 100 = 25%. 20% is the increase as a percentage of the later year.

questions.s: The table shows the marks of six students in a mock test. What is the range of the marks?
questions.e: Range = highest − lowest = 92 − 43 = 49. 92 is the highest value.

questions.s: The table shows four students' marks in three tests. Which student has the lowest total over the three tests?
questions.e: Totals: Faisal 185, Hira 166, Rabia 153, Fatima 229. The lowest is Rabia's, 153.

questions.s: The table shows the number of pupils in three classes and the mean height of each class. What is the mean height of all the pupils taken together, in cm?
questions.e: Weight each mean by its group size: (10×155 + 40×140 + 50×160) ÷ 100 = 15,150 ÷ 100 = 151.5. A simple average of the means ignores the different group sizes. 151.67 averages the three means without weighting.

questions.s: The table shows the sales of a company's four branches in one month. What percentage of the total sales came from the Multan branch?
questions.e: Total sales = 25 + 100 + 175 + 200 = 500 thousand. Share = 25/500 × 100 = 5%. 25% uses the sales figure as the percentage.

questions.s: The table shows the marks scored by 20 students in a quiz. What is the mean mark?
questions.e: Multiply each value by its frequency and add: 2×6 + 3×2 + 4×1 + 5×9 + 6×2 = 79. Divide by the total frequency 20: mean = 3.95. 4 averages the five values without weighting by frequency.

questions.s: The table shows the runs scored by a batter in six matches. What is the batter's mean score per match?
questions.e: Mean = 252 ÷ 6 = 42. 39 is the median, not the mean.

questions.s: The mean of 5 numbers is 59. When one more number is included, the mean rises to 62. What is the new number?
questions.e: Old total = 5 × 59 = 295. New total = 6 × 62 = 372. The new number is 372 − 295 = 77. 62 is the new mean, not the new number.

questions.s: The mean of 5 numbers is 40. 4 of them are 28, 34, 29, 41. What is the remaining number?
questions.e: The total of all 5 numbers is 5 × 40 = 200. The known numbers add up to 132, so the remaining number is 200 − 132 = 68. 40 is the mean itself.

questions.s: What is the median of the values 41, 32, 14, 51, 65, 21, 76, 7?
questions.e: Arrange in order: 7, 14, 21, 32, 41, 51, 65, 76. With 8 values the median is the mean of the two middle values: (32 + 41)/2 = 36.5. 65 is the middle value in the order given, before sorting.

questions.s: The table shows a bank's deposits in four cities. What were the total deposits of Faisalabad over the three years, in Rs million?
questions.e: Add the three years for Faisalabad: 120 + 426 + 285 = 831. 277 is the mean per year.

questions.s: The table shows the number of patients admitted to and discharged from a hospital ward each month. In which month did admissions exceed discharges by the largest number?
questions.e: Find the difference for each month: Jul 6, Aug −13, Sep 11, Oct −1, Nov 19, Dec 36. The largest, 36, is in Dec. Nov has the highest first figure but not the largest difference.

questions.s: The table shows four students' marks in three tests. Which student has the highest mean mark over the three tests?
questions.e: Totals: Mehwish 190, Tariq 239, Bilal 165, Maryam 190. The highest total, and so the highest mean, is Tariq's (239).

questions.s: The table shows the units of four stationery items sold in a month and the price per unit. What was the total revenue from pens and notebooks together, in rupees?
questions.e: Revenue = units × price. Pens: 320 × 37 = 11,840; Notebooks: 360 × 55 = 19,800. Total = Rs 31,640. Rs 680 adds the units sold.

questions.s: The table shows the takings of six shops in a bazaar on one day. What is the difference, in rupees, between the highest and the lowest takings?
questions.e: Range = highest − lowest = 8,800 − 3,500 = 5,300. 8,800 is the highest value.

questions.s: The mean of 8 numbers is 36. When one more number is included, the mean rises to 40. What is the new number?
questions.e: Old total = 8 × 36 = 288. New total = 9 × 40 = 360. The new number is 360 − 288 = 72. 40 is the new mean, not the new number.

questions.s: The mean of 6 numbers is 37. Each number is multiplied by 3 and then 3 is added. What is the mean of the new numbers?
questions.e: Both operations apply to the mean in the same way: 3 × 37 + 3 = 114. 120 adds before multiplying.

questions.s: The mean of 4 numbers is 35. 3 of them are 41, 25, 25. What is the remaining number?
questions.e: The total of all 4 numbers is 4 × 35 = 140. The known numbers add up to 91, so the remaining number is 140 − 91 = 49. 35 is the mean itself.

questions.s: The table shows the number of books issued by a public library. What was the percentage increase from 2020 to 2021?
questions.e: Increase = 780 − 600 = 180. Percentage increase = 180/600 × 100 = 30%. 23.1% is the increase as a percentage of the later year.

questions.s: The marks scored by 7 students in a class test are 15, 9, 55, 25, 23, 22, 19. What is the mean?
questions.e: Mean = sum ÷ number of values = 168 ÷ 7 = 24. 22 is the median.

questions.s: The table shows the number of children in each of 20 families in a street. What is the mean number of children per family?
questions.e: Multiply each value by its frequency and add: 0×6 + 1×3 + 2×7 + 3×2 + 4×2 = 31. Divide by the total frequency 20: mean = 1.55. 2 averages the five values without weighting by frequency.

questions.s: The table shows the number of workers in three factories and the mean daily wage in each. What is the mean daily wage of all the workers taken together, in rupees?

questions.s: The table shows the sales of a company's four branches in one month. What percentage of the total sales came from the Lahore branch?

questions.s: The table shows the number of siblings of each of 31 students. What is the median number of siblings?
questions.e: The median is the value of student number (31 + 1)/2 = 16. Cumulative frequencies are 14, 20, 28, 29, 31, so the 16th student has 1 sibling. 2 is the middle row of the table, not the middle student.

questions.s: A fair six-sided die is rolled once. What is the probability of getting an even number?
questions.e: The even outcomes are 2, 4 and 6, so 3 of the 6 equally likely outcomes are favourable: 3/6 = 1/2. The value 1/6 is the chance of one particular number.

questions.s: Two fair coins are tossed together. What is the probability of getting two heads?
questions.e: There are 4 equally likely outcomes (HH, HT, TH, TT) and only one is HH, so P = 1/4. Counting only 3 outcomes (two heads, one head, no heads) wrongly gives 1/3, because those are not equally likely.

questions.s: A bag holds 3 red balls and 5 blue balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red?

questions.s: One card is drawn at random from a standard pack of 52 cards. What is the probability that it is a king?
questions.e: There are 4 kings among 52 cards, so P = 4/52 = 1/13. The value 1/4 is the chance of drawing a card of one particular suit, and 4/13 divides by the 13 cards of a suit instead of the full pack.

questions.s: The probability that it rains tomorrow in Lahore is 0.35. What is the probability that it does not rain?
questions.e: The probabilities of an event and its complement add to 1, so P(no rain) = 1 − 0.35 = 0.65. The value 0.35 is the probability of rain itself.

questions.s: What is the value of 5!?
In how many ways can 4 different books be arranged in a row on a shelf?
questions.e: The first place has 4 choices, then 3, 2 and 1, so 4! = 24 arrangements. The value 16 is 4², which would allow a book to be used twice.

questions.s: A fair die is rolled once. What is the probability of getting a number greater than 4?
questions.e: The numbers greater than 4 are 5 and 6, which is 2 of 6 outcomes, so P = 2/6 = 1/3. The value 1/6 counts only one of them.

questions.s: Ten tickets are numbered 1 to 10 and one is drawn at random. What is the probability that its number is a multiple of 3?
questions.e: The multiples of 3 are 3, 6 and 9, so 3 of the 10 tickets qualify: P = 3/10. The value 1/3 is the proportion over all positive integers, not over these ten.

questions.s: A canteen offers 3 starters and 4 main dishes. How many different meals of one starter and one main dish can be chosen?
questions.e: Each of the 3 starters can be paired with any of the 4 mains, so 3 × 4 = 12 meals. Adding gives only 7, which counts the dishes rather than the pairs.

questions.s: In how many ways can 2 students be chosen from a group of 5?
questions.e: The order of choosing does not matter, so the count is C(5, 2) = 5 × 4 ÷ 2 = 10. The value 20 counts ordered pairs (5 × 4), and 25 allows the same student twice.

questions.s: A class has 18 boys and 12 girls. One student is chosen at random. What is the probability that the student is a girl?
questions.e: There are 30 students and 12 are girls, so P = 12/30 = 2/5. The value 2/3 is the ratio of girls to boys rather than to all students.

questions.s: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers is 7?
questions.e: Of the 36 equally likely outcomes, six give a sum of 7: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1). So P = 6/36 = 1/6. Counting (3,4) and (4,3) as one outcome would wrongly reduce the number of favourable cases.

questions.s: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers is 9?
questions.e: The outcomes giving 9 are (3,6), (4,5), (5,4) and (6,3), which is 4 of 36, so P = 4/36 = 1/9. A sum of 7 has six outcomes, so 1/6 belongs to that case.

questions.s: A fair coin is tossed three times. What is the probability of getting exactly two heads?
questions.e: There are 2³ = 8 equally likely outcomes, and exactly two heads occur in HHT, HTH and THH, i.e. 3 outcomes. P = 3/8. The value 1/4 counts only one arrangement of the two heads.

questions.s: A bag contains 4 red and 6 blue balls. Two balls are drawn one after the other without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: P(first red) = 4/10 and then P(second red) = 3/9, so P = 4/10 × 3/9 = 12/90 = 2/15. The value 4/25 results from putting the first ball back (4/10 × 4/10), which does not apply here.

questions.s: In how many different ways can the letters of the word LAHORE be arranged?
questions.e: All six letters are different, so there are 6! = 720 arrangements. Dividing by 2 (360) would be right only if two letters were identical.

questions.s: How many different arrangements can be made from all the letters of the word APPLE?
questions.e: There are 5 letters of which P appears twice, so the number of arrangements is 5! ÷ 2! = 120 ÷ 2 = 60. The value 120 treats the two P's as different.

questions.s: A committee of 3 is to be chosen from 7 people. How many different committees are possible?
questions.e: The order does not matter, so C(7, 3) = 7 × 6 × 5 ÷ (3 × 2 × 1) = 35. The value 210 counts ordered selections, i.e. 7 × 6 × 5.

questions.s: A bank card has a 4-digit PIN, each digit from 0 to 9, and digits may repeat. How many different PINs are possible?
questions.e: Each of the 4 positions can take any of 10 digits, so there are 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 = 10,000 PINs. The value 5,040 is the count when no digit may repeat.

questions.s: How many 3-digit numbers can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 if no digit is used more than once?
questions.e: There are 5 choices for the hundreds digit, then 4, then 3, giving 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 numbers. The value 125 allows repeated digits.

questions.s: A fair coin is tossed three times. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
questions.e: The only outcome with no head is TTT, which has probability 1/8, so P(at least one head) = 1 − 1/8 = 7/8. The value 1/8 is the probability of no head at all.

questions.s: One card is drawn from a standard pack of 52 cards. What is the probability that it is a red card or a king?
questions.e: There are 26 red cards and 4 kings, but the 2 red kings are in both groups: 26 + 4 − 2 = 28. So P = 28/52 = 7/13. The value 15/26 (30 cards) forgets to remove the double count.

questions.s: A bag contains 5 red, 3 green and 2 yellow balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is not green?
questions.e: There are 10 balls and 3 are green, so P(not green) = 1 − 3/10 = 7/10. The value 3/10 is the probability of green.

questions.s: At a meeting each of 8 people shakes hands once with every other person. How many handshakes take place?
questions.e: Each handshake involves a pair, and the order does not matter: C(8, 2) = 28. The value 56 counts each handshake twice (8 × 7).

questions.s: A and B are independent events with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.5. What is P(A and B)?
questions.e: For independent events, P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) = 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.2. The sum 0.9 would apply to P(A or B) only if the events could not occur together.

questions.s: For independent events A and B, P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.5. What is the probability that at least one of them occurs?
questions.e: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B) = 0.4 + 0.5 − 0.2 = 0.7. Simply adding gives 0.9, which counts the case where both occur twice.

questions.s: A fair die is rolled twice. What is the probability of getting a six both times?
questions.e: The rolls are independent, so P = 1/6 × 1/6 = 1/36. The value 1/12 adds the probabilities instead of multiplying them.

questions.s: In how many ways can 4 people be selected from a group of 6?
questions.e: The order does not matter, so C(6, 4) = C(6, 2) = 6 × 5 ÷ 2 = 15. The value 360 counts ordered selections (6 × 5 × 4 × 3).

questions.s: A number is chosen at random from the integers 1 to 20. What is the probability that it is prime?
questions.e: The primes up to 20 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19, which is 8 numbers, so P = 8/20 = 2/5. Including 1 as a prime would give 9/20, but 1 is not prime.

questions.s: How many different outcomes are possible when a fair coin is tossed four times?
questions.e: Each toss has 2 outcomes, so there are 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 16 outcomes in all. The value 8 corresponds to three tosses, and 24 is 4!, which counts orderings of four different items.

questions.s: A committee of 3 is to be formed from 4 men and 3 women with exactly 2 men and 1 woman. How many such committees are possible?
questions.e: Choose the 2 men in C(4, 2) = 6 ways and the woman in 3 ways: 6 × 3 = 18. The value 36 counts the two men as an ordered pair (4 × 3 × 3), which counts each committee twice.

questions.s: In how many ways can 5 people be seated in a row if two particular people must sit next to each other?
questions.e: Treat the pair as one block: 4 units can be arranged in 4! = 24 ways, and the two people can swap inside the block in 2 ways. Total = 48. The value 24 forgets the swap, and 120 ignores the restriction.

questions.s: Two cards are drawn one after the other without replacement from a standard pack of 52 cards. What is the probability that both are aces?
questions.e: P(first ace) = 4/52 and P(second ace) = 3/51, so P = 12/2,652 = 1/221. The value 1/169 comes from drawing with replacement (1/13 × 1/13).

questions.s: How many different arrangements are there of all the letters of the word LEVEL?
questions.e: LEVEL has 5 letters with L twice and E twice, so the arrangements number 5! ÷ (2! × 2!) = 120 ÷ 4 = 30. The value 60 divides by only one repeated letter.

questions.s: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is a prime number?
questions.e: The prime sums are 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11, which can occur in 1 + 2 + 4 + 6 + 2 = 15 ways out of 36, so P = 15/36 = 5/12. The value 1/2 would be the probability of an even sum.

questions.s: A bag has 5 red and 4 blue balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that they are of different colours?
questions.e: P(red then blue) = 5/9 × 4/8 = 5/18 and P(blue then red) = 4/9 × 5/8 = 5/18, so P = 5/18 + 5/18 = 5/9. The value 40/81 comes from drawing with replacement.

questions.s: How many even 4-digit numbers can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 if no digit is repeated?
questions.e: The last digit must be 2, 4 or 6 (3 choices). The other three places are filled from the remaining 5 digits in 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 ways, so the total is 3 × 60 = 180. The value 360 ignores the 'even' condition.

questions.s: A committee of 4 is chosen from 5 men and 4 women. In how many ways can it be chosen so that it contains at least one woman?
questions.e: Without restriction there are C(9, 4) = 126 committees. Those with no woman have all 4 chosen from the 5 men: C(5, 4) = 5. So the answer is 126 − 5 = 121. The value 126 includes the all-male committees.

questions.s: A fair coin is tossed 5 times. What is the probability of getting exactly 3 heads?
questions.e: There are 2⁵ = 32 equally likely outcomes and C(5, 3) = 10 of them have exactly 3 heads, so P = 10/32 = 5/16. Counting just one arrangement of the heads would ignore the 10 positions they can take.

questions.s: A bag holds 4 white and 6 black balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is white?
questions.e: There are 10 balls, 4 of them white, so P = 4/10 = 2/5. The value 3/5 is the probability of black, and 2/3 compares white with black.

questions.s: What is the value of 6! ÷ 4!?
questions.e: 6! ÷ 4! = (6 × 5 × 4!) ÷ 4! = 6 × 5 = 30. The value 15 is C(6, 2), which would need a further division by 2!.

questions.s: A fair die is rolled once. What is the probability of getting a 7?
questions.e: A die shows only 1 to 6, so a 7 is impossible and its probability is 0. A probability of 1 would mean it is certain.

questions.s: There are 3 roads from town A to town B and 2 roads from town B to town C. How many different routes lead from A to C through B?
questions.e: Each of the 3 roads to B can be followed by either of the 2 roads to C, so 3 × 2 = 6 routes. Adding the roads (5) gives the total number of roads, not the number of routes.

questions.s: The probability that a candidate passes a test is 3/5. What is the probability that the candidate fails?
questions.e: Passing and failing are complementary, so P(fail) = 1 − 3/5 = 2/5. A probability can never be above 1, so 5/3 is impossible.

questions.s: One card is drawn from a standard pack. What is the probability that it is a face card (jack, queen or king)?
questions.e: There are 3 face cards in each of 4 suits, so 12 of the 52 cards: 12/52 = 3/13. The value 1/13 would be correct for a single rank such as kings.

questions.s: A bag has 3 red and 2 blue balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are blue?
questions.e: P(first blue) = 2/5 and then P(second blue) = 1/4, so P = 2/20 = 1/10. The value 4/25 comes from replacing the first ball.

questions.s: In how many ways can 3 books be chosen from 8 different books?
questions.e: The order does not matter, so C(8, 3) = 8 × 7 × 6 ÷ 6 = 56. The value 336 counts ordered selections.

questions.s: How many different arrangements can be made from all the letters of the word MAMA?
questions.e: There are 4 letters with M twice and A twice, so 4! ÷ (2! × 2!) = 24 ÷ 4 = 6. The value 12 divides by only one pair of repeated letters.

questions.s: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 8?
questions.e: The sum 8 occurs for (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3) and (6,2): 5 of 36 outcomes. The value 2/9 equals 8/36 and mixes up the target sum with the number of outcomes.

questions.s: A and B are independent events with P(A) = 1/3 and P(B) = 1/4. What is P(A and B)?
questions.e: For independent events, multiply: 1/3 × 1/4 = 1/12. The value 7/12 is their sum, which is not the probability of both occurring.

questions.s: How many 3-digit numbers can be formed using the digits 0 to 9 if all three digits are different and the first digit cannot be 0?
questions.e: The first digit has 9 choices (1–9), the second has 9 (0 and the remaining 8 digits), and the third has 8, so the count is 9 × 9 × 8 = 648. The value 720 allows a leading zero.

questions.s: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that at least one of them shows a six?
questions.e: P(no six) = 5/6 × 5/6 = 25/36, so P(at least one six) = 1 − 25/36 = 11/36. Adding 1/6 + 1/6 = 1/3 counts the (6,6) outcome twice.

questions.s: In how many ways can 6 people be seated around a circular table, if only their positions relative to each other matter?
questions.e: Fix one person to remove rotations; the other 5 can be arranged in 5! = 120 ways. The value 720 would be right for seats in a row.

questions.s: A box has 4 red, 3 green and 3 blue balls. Three balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that all three are of the same colour?
questions.e: The favourable selections are C(4, 3) + C(3, 3) + C(3, 3) = 4 + 1 + 1 = 6, out of C(10, 3) = 120, so P = 6/120 = 1/20. Counting only the red balls as 'same colour' would give 4/120 = 1/30.
